37.0   FRIENDLY TAX REGIME FOR SSI
37.1   The various taxes, incentives / exemptions which actually affect the working of small scale units are excise duties,
customs duties, income tax, service tax, sales tax (central sales tax as well as state level sales tax), octroi, stamp duties,
CENVAT (earlier MODVAT), local an municipal taxes, etc. The announcements made by the Union Finance Minister
in his Budget Speech 2004-05 would have a positive impact on the SSI sector, particularly the announcements like
enhancing the ceiling for loans under the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme from Rs. 40 lakh to Rs. l crore and
raising the rate of subsidy from 12 per cent to 15 per cent. The scope of the scheme will be enlarged by adding more
sub-sectors and technologies eligible for assistance. A large number of units producing certain items whose investment
ceiling has been raised to Rs.5 crore over the past few years, would benefit from this enhancement of the credit limit and
subsidy rate. The Scheme would also become popular with the new provisions. The units in the Drugs and
Pharmaceuticals sector have to comply with Schedule ‘M’ of the Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Rules, 1945 which inter
alia, incorporate “Good Manufacturing Practices” (GMP) and to make considerable investments by December, 2004.
Such units would benefit from the increased limits under the CLCSS.

          (i)    SSI units will be encouraged to obtain credit rating; A Scheme on Credit Rating for SSI units, exclusively
tailored to meet their requirements, will be formulated by the Government soon. The credit rating facility
would help in improving the flow of credit to SSI sector by reducing/minimizing the risk perception of the
banks towards the SSI units.

38.0   IMPACT OF WTO PROVISIONS ON VARIOUS SECTORS OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
38.1   Government is constantly assessing and monitoring the impact of the removal of Quantitative Restrictions (QRs)
and Globalization on the growth and development of Small Scale Industries (SSIs) in the country. Though removal of
QRs have exposed the SSIs to a greater competition, yet the SSI sector has continued to grow. However, even after the
removal of QRs, protection to the industries is available in the form of raising custom duties upto the bound levels,
imposing anti-dumping duties, taking safeguards measures in case of surge in imports, etc.
38.2   Removal of QRs does not automatically remove all the protection available to the domestic producers. India can
regulate imports through adjustments in tariff within the bound rates. Apart from tariff, action under anti-dumping and
safeguard measures can be taken to provide protection to the domestic producers. For initiating anti-dumping action and
imposition of safeguard duty, separate Directorates are already working under the Ministry of Commerce and the

153rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/153rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:50:22]
Ministry of Finance respectively.
38.3   As on May, 2004 final anti-dumping duty has been imposed on 143 items, preliminary duty has been imposed on
5 items and 10 cases are under investigation. DG (AD) has imposed final duties on dry batteries and sports goods after
initiating suo moto investigations. The Director General of Safeguards has taken up action in respect of 15 products for
investigations. So far, safeguard duties in respect of 8 cases have been imposed. The Government are also in the process
of amending the provisions of Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 so that safeguard action in the
form of Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) could be applied if there are sudden and massive imports. The Government can
also specify standards, impose conditions for reasons of public, plant & animal health, security and public morality on
goods entering India.
38.4   The Government has put in place several measures to help small enterprises become globally competitive. These
include special focus on areas such as technology upgradation, infrastructure assistance through the cluster approach,
timely availability of credit, adoption of modern management practices, use of electronic infrastructure and other IT
applications, marketing and timely information dissemination, including sensitisation of small industries to the emerging
challenges of trade liberalization. Government is fully aware of the WTO environment and is taking appropriate
measures for preparing the Small Scale Sector to meet the challenges of liberalization/globalization. Taking a view of
the whole situation, a new SSI policy including certain new schemes/incentives were announced during the National
Conference on SSI held at New Delhi 30-31 August 2000. Some of the major incentives/ measures include raising the
excise exemption limit from Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. l crore, a scheme of Capital Subsidy of 12 per cent for investment in
technology upgradation in select sectors, raising the eligibility limit for coverage under the Credit Guarantee Scheme
from Rs.10 lakhs to 25 lakhs, continuation of financial support (up to 75,000) for obtaining ISO 9000/ISO14001
certification up to the end of 10th Plan.
38.5   The WTO Agreement contains a number of provisions and annexes that have an impact on the industry. It has not
been found feasible to monitor the detailed impact of these agreements sector-specific and cluster-specific. However,
industrial units are encouraged to bring to the notice of Office of the DC(SSI) either of their-own or through the
associations so that the aspects of the WTO agreement that are not found suitable to them are brought to the notice of
Ministry of Commerce and Industry to take appropriate action in the matter.
38.6   The Committee is pleased to note that the Government is well aware of the WTO environment and taking
measures for preparing SSI sector to meet the challenges of globalization and liberalization under the WTO
regime. However, the basic concern of the Committee is the protection and promotion of domestic SSI sector
under the prevailing global market economy. Therefore, the continuous and concrete efforts should be made by
the Government to protect the domestic Small Scale Industries from the on-slaught of adverse impact of
globalization and liberalization through appropriate tariff adjustment, anti-dumping measures and other
safeguards. Simultaneously the process of strengthening SSI sector and acquiring the requisite competitive
resilience should be enhanced on the ground level.
39.0   LEGAL FRAMEWORK
39.1   At present Small Scale Industries are governed by Industries (Development & Regulation) Act, 1951. However
the Acts/rules and regulations are formulated by various authorities at the Central Government, State Government level
and Local authorities. These legal regulations can be classified into, labour related issues, tax related issues, finance
related issues, location related issues, product related issues, environment related issues and safety, security, hygiene,
health and welfare related issues, etc.
39.2   The regulatory frame work, particularly pertaining to Labour related Laws is cumbersome and in this regard the
plethora of laws, rules and regulations that have accumulated over the last several years of control regimes have become
truly oppressive. The burden of inspections under various laws has proved to be too onerous to bear. They have adverse
bearing on the promotion and development of Small Scale Industries.
39.3   All the industries including Large, Medium and Small Scale mentioned in schedule I of the ID&R Act, fall under
the purview of Industrial Development and Regulation (IDR) Act, 1951. However, those units employing 50/100 or less
workers , with /without power do not fall under the purview of ID&R Act. A plethora of laws, rules and regulations and
the burden of inspections have crippled the SSI Sector. Therefore with a view to simplify these laws, rules and
regulations and streamline the system of inspections, Small Enterprises Development Bill (Single Law for SSIs) is
proposed to be enacted. It will apply only to Small Scale Sector and contains inter-alia, provisions to simplify existing
Labour Laws and streamline inspections, to wipe out the tyranny of Inspector Raj.
39.4   The Committee desires that legal framework affecting the Small Scale Industries must be satisfactory in order to
give fillip to the promotion and development of Small Scale Industries. The following issues may be taken up on

153rd Report of Committee on Industry

priority basis and the Ministry of SSI should pursue with the concerned Ministries :-
          (i)    A single Unified Act governing the rules pertaining to retrenchment and layoffs and social benefits for
employees.
          (ii)    Enactment of Single Comprehensive Small Enterprises Development Act for SSEs similar to the
Industrial Development and Regulation (IDR) Act.
          (iii)   Comprehensive Social Security Scheme for widening the social safety nets.
          (iv)   Since the Inspector Raj is causing severe harassment to Small Scale Units progress made for suitable
legislation for giving good bye to Inspector Raj to wipe out the tyranny of Inspector Raj.
40.0   INDIAN MODEL OF SSI SECTOR VIS-A-VIS MODEL OF SSI SECTORS IN THE WORLD
40.1   At present all industries with an investment upto Rs. 1 (one) crore in Plant and Machinery whether held on
ownership term or on lease or by hire purchase come under the purview of this Ministry. This limit in respect of 41
items covering hosiery, Pharmaceuticals, Stationery and hand tools has been enhanced to Rs. 5.00 crore. Further in 1991
Government also decided to extend the benefit being enjoyed by the SSIs to some of the industry-related service and
business enterprises with investment in fixed assets, (excluding land and building) upto Rs. 10.00 lakhs irrespective of
the location of the units.
40.2   The Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC) had recommended that the inclusion of services and the
enlargement of the scope of the Ministry to medium establishment are important in the context of the emergence of
sunrise knowledge-based industries as the harbinger of a new industrial revolution. New knowledge-based industries
like pharmaceuticals and biotechnology industries have to be internationally competitive and will require
encouragement and support in the initial period of their development. The emergence of IT and of software in a large
way in this country also suggests the need for bringing the service sector prominently into the ambit of encouragement
and support given to small and medium establishments and the Ministry may be renamed as the Ministry of Small and
Medium Establishments.
40.3   The ERC was of the view that to provide an environment for the natural growth of small establishments, the
industrial establishments (including the service sector) be divided into the following four categories on the basis of
investment limits.
 (i) Tiny Upto Rs. 25.00 lakh
(ii) Small Above Rs. 25.00 lakh & upto Rs. 5.00 crore
(iii) Medium; and Above Rs. 5.00 crore & upto Rs. 10.00 crore
(iv) Large Above Rs. 10.00 crore

          (iii)   Freedom from the plethora of rules and regulations existing in the SSI sector, which is known as
Inspector Raj;
          (iv)   Full support to the service industry to fulfill its true growth and employment generation potential;
and
          (v)   Training of existing and potential entrepreneurs and workers on a massive scale. Modern management
practices and skill up-gradation through advanced training facilities for capacity building in the SSI
sector.

153rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/153rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:50:22]
OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE
COMMITTEE — AT A GLANCE
SERVICE AUDITING OF ORGANS UNDER THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
          The Committee recommends that the Government should undertake steps for service auditing of organs under the
Ministry of Small Scale Industries so that their delivery system can be improved for the betterment of small scale
industries.          (Para 2.1)
          The Committee observes that SSI sector is a major manufacturing sector contributing substantially to the export
and employment generation. This sector needs a boost which can largely come from the Government. A reduction of
allocation to the extent of 57 per cent of the Ministry’s requirement will adverse affect the growth of SSI sector. The
Committee therefore impresses upon the Government to provide necessary funds at RE stage.                                (Para
3.1)
TARGETS SET BY THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES FOR TENTHS FIVE YEAR PLAN
          The Committee is of the view that the growth in production, employment and exports contributes to national
economic development and progress. The performance of SSI sector with regard to the production reveals that it could
so far achieve merely 37 per cent to 38 per cent of the targets. The Committee therefore calls upon the Government to
look into this and come out with concrete suggestions so as to enhance the out put as this sector has been assigned an
annual growth target of 12 per cent against 8 per cent for the economy as a whole.
                                                                                                                                             (Para 4.3)
GRANTS TO NATIONAL SMALL INDUSTRIES CORPORATION FOR DEVELOPMENT OF SMALL
SCALE INDUSTRIES
          The Committee recommends that the following measures may be undertaken for making NSIC in fulfilling
its role more effectively: -
          (i)    Flexibility to the NSIC Board to induct professionals in order to build the internal competency levels;
          (ii)   NSIC should be declared a nodal agency for purchases by Government Departments/Agencies. This
will enable NSIC to play an effective role in marketing the products of the SSI sector; and
          (iii) NSIC should be treated at par with SSIDCs in matters relating to allocation of Steel and other raw
materials. At present, allocation of steel is made to NSIC only in those states where SSIDCs do not
exist.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 11.3)
CREDIT LINKED CAPITAL SUBSIDY SCHEME
          The Committee observes that Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme is a very good scheme aimed at
technological up-gradation in SSI sector. The progress so far has been very tardy and in fact the scheme is yet to take
off. The Committee commend the announcements made in the budget speech (2004-05) and hopes that it would show
better results. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry of SSI to provide better package incentives to SSI units for
technology up-gradation and work out an effective strategy.                                                                                       (Para
16.9)
          The Committee recommends that government should undertake the following steps for improving the
functioning of credit linked capital subsidy:----
          (i)    Organising awareness programmes at various location all over the country to increase the awareness
level of industry association, banks, SIDBI and Industry Departments of respective States;
          (ii)   Review of progress of the scheme in meetings State Level Bankers Committees (SLBCs);
          (iii)  Incorporating inputs on the scheme into in service training courses of Bank Managers; and
          (iv)  Publicity measures to increase general awareness about the scheme.
                                                                                                                                         (Para 16.10)
LOAN LIMIT UNDER THE CREDIT GUARANTEE SCHEME
          The Committee observes that loan limit of Rs. 25 lakh for investment in plant and machinery under the Credit
Guarantee Scheme is not sufficient so the loan limit needs to be enhanced at least to Rs. 1 crore. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry of SSI to review the present limit with all concerned and raise the loan limit to
the desired level.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 20.2)

153rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/153rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:50:22]
CREDIT GUARANTEE FUND SCHEME
          The Committee is constrained to observe that despite the provision of the loans up to 25.00 lakh without
collateral/third party guarantee and the guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India thereto, Banks insists on the collateral
security and the third party guarantee and despite the Committee’s repeated recommendation to change the mind set of
the Branch Manager, nothing fruitful has come out. The Committee also notes that the Trust has been making concerted
efforts to create awareness about the Scheme among the Branch Managers of the banks by organizing regional/zonal
based Workshops-cum-Training Programmes where the information relating to the Scheme and the benefits available
are explained in detail. There is however, absence of mechanism assessing the impact of success of credit guarantee
scheme. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry to ensure the success of this
scheme.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                           (Para 22.3)
          The Committee further observes that the credit guarantee fund scheme gets further rough whether due to high
upfront charges of banks like service charge, processing fee and that too differing from bank to bank. Under this scheme
also one time Guarantee Fee of 2.5 per cent of the sanctioned amount and 1 per cent Service Fee on the outstanding loan
is collected as on 31 st March each year. These fees are however, fixed and do not vary from bank to bank. The
Committee feels that this fee should further be reduced and recommends that the Ministry of SSI should take up
necessary action in this regard.         (Para 22.4)
          The Committee observes that it is desirable that the Government expeditiously fulfills its commitment towards
building the Corpus of Rs. 2500 crore with a view to enhance the comfort level of Members Lending Institutions (MLIs)
participating in the Scheme. With the building of adequate corpus fund, the fears of MLIs could be allayed as still some
of the banks have reservations about the Scheme because of their bad experience in the past with a similar scheme
operated by the RBI.  
                                                                                                                                           (Para 22.9)
LUMP SUM PROVISION FOR PROJECTS/SCHEMES FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE NORTH EASTERN
AREAS AND SIKKIM
          The Committee hopes that the actions expected to be taken during 2004-05 in the North East Region by NSIC
would prove instrumental in employment generation and poverty alleviation in the region.                 (Para 23.5)
TINY AND MICRO ENTERPRISES
          The Committee recommends that effective measures must be taken for (i) better importing of entrepreneurs skills
and training, (ii) acquiring marketing techniques (iii) Access to appropriate technology (iv) strengthening capital base
and institutional credit and (v) providing infrastructural facilities.                                                   (Para 25.3)
CREDIT RATING
          The Committee strongly recommends for a Credit Rating Mechanism covering both the credit and performance
factors. The Committee accordingly recommends the Ministry to expedite the process of initiating and popularizing the
Credit Rating System for SSI units.                                                                                                           (Para 26.2)
TECHNOLOGY UPGRADATION IN SSI SECTOR
          The Committee recommends that the Ministry of SSI should chalk out action plan for promoting Public -Private
partnership for technology up-gradation in SSI sector. The Committee is of the considered view that Public-Private
partnership would give the requisite boost to the technology up-gradation in the SSI sector.                    (Para 27.2)
POLICY OF DE-RESERVATION IN SSI SECTOR
          The Committee is of the view that reservation of items to SSI sector should not become a restriction to the growth
of this sector as far as investment and technology upgradation is concerned. The Committee, however, strongly, feels
that Government should take precaution while taking out an item from the reserved list so that labour oriented units
remain protected.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 28.3)
ADOPTION OF “BEST PRACTICES CODE”
          The Committee is of the view that there is a need for amendment in the provision of the Delayed Payment Small
Scale and Ancillary Industrial Undertaking Act 1993 as amended in 1998 and the relevant provisions of the Companies
Act i.e. mandatory provision requiring the large enterprises to show in the entries of their Balance sheets the amount due
for payment to the SSI units to enable SSI units/suppliers to get payments as agreed upon. The Committee, therefore,

153rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/153rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:50:22]
recommends that the Government should come out with the requisite amendment in the said Act without further delay.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 29.2)
PROGRESS IN REGARD TO ENACTMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP ACT
          The Committee is in agreement with the view of the Ministry of SSI that the SSI sector needs the Limited
Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of SSI should continue to pursue for
legislation of the Limited Liability Partnership Act in the interest of Small Scale Sector.                                              
(Para 30.2)
SUNRISE INDUSTRIES IN THE SSI SECTOR
          The Committee desires that adequate steps should be taken to identify the sunrise industries in the SSI sector e.g.
Information Technology (IT), Biotechnology (BT) Pharmaceuticals and Nano-technologies along with IT Enabled
Services (ITES) and concrete steps may be undertaken to reinforce appropriate policy regime to promote sunrise SSI
industries which have the potential to be the winners of tomorrow. The issue such as IPR protectionand management of
rapid up-scaling of operations could be taken up on priority basis.                                                                     (Para 31.3)
STREAMLINING AND STRENGTHENING THE ANTI-DUMPING MECHANISM
          The Committee desires that the Ministry of SSI should make efforts for ensuring the following things:----
          (i)    Working of renewed provision in Indo-Nepal Treaty in Trade Transit w.e.f. 6 th March, 2002, in
checking influx of Chinese goods en-route Nepal;
          (ii)   Conversion of Quantitative restriction (QRs) into rationalised tariff regime for providing protection to
the domestic SSIs;
          (iii)  Rationalisation of countervailing duties and safeguard duties to protect domestic producers in
consonance with WTO provision; and
          (iv)  Expeditious disposal dumping cases are anti-dumping actions thereto, in view of almost all SSI
products under open general license (OGL) list.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 32.4)
PURCHASE PREFERENCE FOR SSI
          The Committee desires that the issue of Procurement Policy & Price Preference Policy for promotion of
Small Entrepreneurs should be incorporated in the proposed legislation for Small Enterprises Development. 
(Para 33.3)
WORKING GROUP ON REHABILITATION OF SICK UNITS
          The Committee desires that the Ministry of Small Scale Industries should undertake concrete steps for
ensuring following things:-
          (i)     arresting the mortality rate in SSI sector and extending sufficient credit facilities to SSI units;
          (ii)    insertion of an arbitration clause in the borrower lender agreement in terms of Indian Arbitration Act
in the Banking Ombudsman Scheme, 2002;
          (iii)   effective outcome of efforts made for Sick Units Rehabilitation Committee;
          (iv)   result oriented outcome of efforts made by State-level Inter Institutional and Committee’s (SLIICs) in
regard to avoiding delay in rehabilitations;
          (v)    expeditious Progress made in regard to setting up of Local Committees between State Government,
SSI Associations and Banks to sort out credit related issues at local level; and
          (vi)   representation of SSI Associations in the Rehabilitation Cell.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 35.4)
Credit flow to SSI Sector
          The Committee hopes that implementation the S.P. Gupta Committee’s recommendations in regard to credit flow
to SSI sector by pubic sector Banks to facilitate additional capacity generation, expansion of existing units and
improving capacity utilization diversification and to enhance competitiveness of SSI sectors would fetch positive result
for Small Scale Industries. The Ministry of Small Scale Industries for the furtherance and proliferation may emphasize
the following steps.
          (i)     popularisation of venture capital funding to SSI units;
          (ii)    strengthening credit delivery system and support services agencies;
          (iii)   furtherance and strengthening of Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) for extending
financial and support services to SSIs;

153rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/153rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:50:22]
          (iv)   enhancing the net percentage of credit to Small Scale Industries vis-a-vis the large Scale Industries;
          (v)    effective steps for Restructuring of State Financial Corporations (SFCs);
          (vi)   steps for enhancing flow of additional credit for SSI sector;
          (vii)  reinforcing Technology Bank for SME up-gradation to facilitate technology transfer project
evaluation, risks management etc.;
          (viii)re-orienting the role of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) for extending credit flow to rural Small Scale
Industries;
          (ix)   introducing and encouraging Laghu Udyog Credit Cards ; and
          (x)    extending sufficient financial assistance extended to Self Help Groups.
                                                                                                                                         (Para 36.11)
FRIENDLY TAX REGIME FOR SSI
          The Committee desires that the Ministry of SSI should take initiatives/ measures for SSI friendly tax regime and
other fiscal measure required to promote SSI at an accelerated pace keeping in view the on going liberalization and
globalization process and the need to protect the domestic SSI Sector. In order to promote the SSI sector, certain fiscal
measures need to be taken to establish a SSI-friendly tax regime.
          (i)     Extension of General SSI Excise Exemption to SSI units manufacturing branded goods in urban
areas, as available in rural areas.
          (ii)    Increase in the excise exemption from Rs. l crore to Rs. 2 crore to new as well as existing SSI units in
rural as well as urban areas.
          (iii)   To increase the turnover eligibility limit for availing the General SSI Excise Exemption from Rs.3
crore to Rs.5 crore.
          (iv)   Lower rates of excise duties on items having large presence of SSI units in their manufacturing.
          (v)    Rationalisation of custom duties in cases involving raw material and finished products for the same
product category.
          (vi)   Lower custom duties on import of raw material (basic raw material and intermediate goods) and
higher duties on finished products.
          (vii)  Incentives to facilitate exports by the SSI units.
          (viii)In order to induce SSI Sector to undertake technology upgradation, excise and customs duty
relief/concession be provided to SSIs on purchase of new plant and machinery for technology
upgradation.
          (ix)   Incentives for ancillarisation so as to establish better linkages between the large and small industries.
          (x)    Once concession/new fiscal provision is announced, it should be maintained for at least three years in
order to maintain continuity and growth.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 37.5)
IMPACT OF WTO PROVISIONS ON VARIOUS SECTORS OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
          The Committee is pleased to note that the Government is/aware of the WTO environment and taking measures for
preparing SSI sector to meet the challenges of globalization and liberalization under the WTO regime. However, the
basic concern of the Committee is the protection and promotion of domestic SSI sector under the prevailing global
market economy. Therefore, the continuous and concrete efforts should be made by the Government to protect the
domestic Small Scale Industries from the on-slaught of adverse impact of globalization and liberalization through
appropriate tariff adjustment, anti dumping measures and other safeguards. Simultaneously the process of strengthening
SSI sector and acquiring the requisite competitive resilience should be enhanced on the ground
level.                                                              
                                                                                                                                           (Para 38.6)
LEGAL FRAMEWORK
          The Committee desires that legal framework affecting the Small Scale Industries must be satisfactory in order to
give fillip to the promotion and development of Small Scale Industries. The following issues may be taken up on
priority basis and the Ministry of SSI should pursue with the concerned Ministries:----

153rd Report of Committee on Industry

          (i)    A single Unified Act governing the rules pertaining to retrenchment and layoffs and social benefits for
employees.
          (ii)   Enactment of Single Comprehensive Small Enterprises Development Act for SSEs similar to the
Industrial Development and Regulation (IDR) Act.
          (iii)  Comprehensive Social Security Scheme for widening the social safety nets.
          (iv)  Since the Inspector Raj is causing severe harassment to Small Scale Units progress made for suitable
legislation for giving good bye to Inspector Raj to wipe out the tyranny of Inspector Raj.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 39.4)
INDIAN MODEL OF SSI SECTOR VIS-A-VIS MODEL OF SSI SECTORS IN THE WORLD
          The Committee notes that the announcement of the Finance Minister in the budget for 2004-05, that there is need
to provide some space for SSIs to grow into medium enterprises. The Committee is in agreement with the
announcement of the Finance Minister in the General Budget (2004-05) that small scale industries is the engine of
growth, therefore, SSI units must be given the space to grow into medium enterprises. In the context of globalisation
there is a growing feeling in certain quarters that India should also adopt the SME Concept World over, policies are
devised to meet the requirement of small and medium enterprises (SME). The Committee desires that the steps should
be initiated for formulating policies for Medium Enterprises and adequate institutional arrangement and mechanism
should be setup for working of medium enterprises in the national
economy.                                                                                                                            (Para 40.6)
          The Committee is in agreement with the recommendation of ERC and directs that the Government should
consider for raising the limit of SSI sector from existing Rs. 1 crore to Rs.5 crore for all items keeping in view inflation
rate and the requirement for setting up small scale units.                                                                           (Para 40.7)
          The Committee further recommends that for streamlining and strengthening the contribution of SSI sector
in the national economy, the Government the should focus on the following issues:----
          (i)    Providing full credit, technology up-gradation, modernization and marketing support to the SSI
sector;
          (ii)   Infrastructure upgradation in general particularly in the major SSI industrial clusters;
          (iii)  Freedom from the plethora of rules and regulations existing in the SSI sector, which is known as
Inspector Raj;
          (iv)  Full support to the service industry to fulfill its true growth and employment generation potential; and
          (v)   Training of existing and potential entrepreneurs and workers on a massive scale. Modern management
practices and skill up-gradation through advanced training facilities for capacity building in the SSI
sector.

REPORT
          The Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry deals with the Action
Taken by the Government on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s 129 th Report on the Credit Flow to
SSI Sector in the Regions of Delhi, Noida and Ghaziabad pertaining to the Ministry of Small Scale Industries. The said
Report was presented to Rajya Sabha on the 19 th August, 2003 and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 21 st August,
2003.
2.       Action Taken Notes were received from the Government in respect of the recommendations contained in the
129th Report. They have been categorized as follows:
          (i)    Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government: 5.4, 5.9 and 5.13. (Chapter-
I).
          (ii)    Recommendations/Observations, which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the
Government’s replies: 5,1, 5.5, 5.6, 5.8, 5.11, 5.12, 5.15 and 5.16 (Chapter-II). 
          (iii)   Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted the replies of the
Government: 5.2, 5.3, 5.10 and 5.14 (Chapter-III).
          (iv)   Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of theGovernment have not been received: 5.7
(Chapter-IV).
          (v)   Observations/Recommendations at a Glance (Chapter-V). The Committee is pleased to observe that the
Ministry of Small Scale Industries has accepted its recommendations as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
4.       In respect of recommendations made in Para 5.12, 5.15 and 5.16 in Chapter-II the Committee is convinced with
the logic and explanation advocated by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries and therefore does not want to pursue
further.
5.       The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendation contained in Chapter-III
and therefore the Committee desires that the Ministry of Small Scale Industries should furnish logical explanation in
respect of these recommendations.
6.       In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry of Small Scale Industries has either furnished
the interim replies or couched its language in vague terms like noted for compliance guidance, therefore, the Committee
desires that the Ministry of Small Scale Industries should furnish Action Taken Notes in respect of recommendations
categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the
Committee.
7.       The details of the Action Taken is being discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1     Regular Flow of Funds for SSIs
1.1.1  Observation/Recommendation
          In order to ensure that there is no let up in the regular flow of funds for SSIs, the Committee recommends that
there should be enhancement in the quantum of composite loans; removal of procedural difficulties in the path of SSI
advances; sorting out issues relating to mortgages of land including removal of stamp duty and permitting equitable
mortgages, allowing access to low-cost funds to Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) for refinancing
SSI loans.(Para 5.4)
1.1.2  Action Taken/Comments
          In the review meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee held on 2 nd June, 2003, the banks had agreed to
enhance the limit of composite loan from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh. Accordingly, a majority of the Public Sector Banks
have since issued necessary instructions regarding enhancing composite loan limit for SSIs to Rs.50 lakh. As regards,
removal of procedural difficulties for SSI advances, apart from simplification of loan applications and simplification in
procedure for computation of working capital on the basis of 20 per cent of the projected annual turnover, the RBI has
laid down time limits to ensure timely disbursement of loans stipulating that all loan applications upto Rs. 25,000/-
should be disposed off within two weeks and in other cases for loans up to Rs. 5 lakh within a period of four weeks,
provided the loan applications are complete in all respects. As already indicated, removal of stamp duty on land
mortgages, etc. come under the purview of the respective State Governments. For allowing access to low cost funds to
SIDBI for refinancing SSI loans, SIDBI is constantly pursuing with the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
Recently, the Hon’ble Finance Minister has made an announcement regarding creation of a Small and Medium
Enterprises (SME) Fund of Rs. 10,000 crore by SIDBI for making available credit to small and medium enterprises at
200 basis points below PLR.
1.2     Soft Loans to SSIs
1.2.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Government has specifically targeted the core issue of providing soft loans to SSIs, at lower rates of interest
to ensure the viability and make them most market insistent for their sustainability. The Committee recommends that the
Public sector banks should be advised to strictly follow the guidelines of the Government of India, Ministry of Finance
and Reserve Bank of India in regard to increasing SSI sector advance and facilitating industrial growth. The Committee
opines that flagrant violation of such directions/guidelines should be made penal offence.                                               
(Para 5.9)
1.2.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The Bank rate changes by the RBI combined with Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and repo rate changes have
emerged as signalling device for interest rate changes The reduction in Bank rate announced in the statements on
Monetary and Credit Policy or outside the policy from time to time has resulted in a consequential reduction in the
lending rates. Banks have now the flexibility to offer lending rates on a fixed rate or on a floating rate. The reduction in
interest rates and the offer of floating rates will help the SSI units to procure funds at lower costs than what was
prevailing in earlier years. Banks have been advised that they may set the interest rate on advances to SSI sector keeping
in view prevailing general southward movement in interest rates. Furthermore, as per the announcement made by the
Hon’ble Finance Minister in the Union Budget 2003-04, banks are also required to adopt the interest rate band of 2 per
cent above and below their respective Prime Lending Rates (PLRs) for secured advances. Further, as per the decision
arrived at the meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee, banks have been advised that they may examine having at
least 3 slabs for rate of interest for advances up to Rs. 50,000, between Rs. 50,000 to Rs.2 lakh and above Rs. 2 lakh.
1.3     Role of RBI for ensuring smooth Credit Flow to SSI Sector
1.3.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee has indicated the commendable role of RBI for ensuring smooth credit flow to SSI sector. The
RBI setup the Nayak Committee in 1991 to advise upon the aspects of adequacy and timeliness of credit to SSI. In its
report submitted in September, 1992, the Committee suggested to implement the several recommendations such as
granting of working capital credit to SSI units to be computed on basis of a minimum of 20 per cent of their projected

annual turnover; giving preference to village industries, tiny industries and other small scale units while meeting credit
requirement sector; extension of Single Window Scheme of SBI to all districts; avoidance of delay in sanctioning and
disbursement of credit to SSI sector; non-insistence on compulsory deposit as a quid-pro-quo for sanctioning the credit
limit, opening of specialized branches; identification of sick units and urgent action to put them on the nursing
programme, the standardized loan application forms to be used by SSI units; imparting of necessary training to Bank
staff to handle the SSI clients. The Committee impress upon the Government that the recommendations of the Nayak
Committee should be adhered to by all the Banks.           (Para 5.13)
1.3.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The RBI has informed that the banks have been advised time and again for adhering to the stipulated norms for
computing working capital on the basis of Nayak Committee recommendations. It has also been clarified to the banks
that the norm of 20 per cent of the projected annual turnover is the minimum limit and that the banks are free to sanction
higher working capital limits at their discretion to SSIs requiring aggregate fund based capital upto Rs. 5 crore from the
banking sector. The banks are also required to arrive at a realistic projection of the turnover based on proper evaluation
of the past trends and future business prospects. Based on the deliberations at the meeting of Standing Advisory
Committee on SSI, banks have been again advised reiterating the instructions on computation of working capital limits.
The RBI has also advised the banks to extend their reach to the SSI sector by bringing in increasing number of tiny units
presently outside the banking reach, within the ambit of bank finance.
1.3.3  The RBI’s studies of Specialised SSI branches as also a few general branches (where sizeable advances are for
SSIs) revealed that banks were adhering to norms of Nayak Committee.

CHAPTER -II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE
IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
2.1     Measures for Enabling SSI Units to have access to Bank Finance
2.1.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee strongly feels that the Government should undertake following measures for enabling SSI units to
have access to bank finance:----
          (i)     To infuse customer friendly approach, undertaking of orientation course and adequate training for staff /
officers of commercial banks for a change in their attitude on lending to SSI sector;
          (ii)     Elimination of plethora of rules and requirements and thereby simplification of procedures for obtaining
credit from Banks. Arrangement may be made for land mortgage instead of stamp duty for enabling SSI units
to obtaining credit from bank against land mortgage;
          (iii)    Paternalistic Government umbrella for development of services through appropriate policy
prescription/legislative changes to ease the problems relating to stamp duty, registration;
          (iv)    Recapitalisation and revamping of State Financial Corporation (SFCs) with the help of SIDBI and IDBI
enabling SFCs to lend fixed capital to SSI units.
                                                                                                                                                      (Para 5.1)
2.1.2  Action Taken/Comments
          Regular training programmes are organized by the banks for infusing-customer friendly approach among the bank
officials. Furthermore, in pursuance to the decisions taken at the meeting of the Department Related Parliamentary
Committee held with the officials of banks/financial institutions during its study visit to Mumbai in June, 2001, RBI has
advised all the banks to conduct entrepreneurship development training programmes and also give exhaustive training to
their staff members for sensitizing them towards the needs of the SSI sector. The feedback received from the banks
reveals that several steps have been taken by banks in this regard.
          (i)     The application forms for loans have been made simple based on the Nayak Committee recommendations
and there is continuous endeavour to simplify the procedure further Computation of credit needs has also
been made simple by computing it on the basis of 20 per cent of the projected annual turnover in respect of
loans upto Rs. 5 crore. The banks have also been advised in July, 2001 that an effective monitoring system
may be put in place for capturing the entire process of sanctioning of loan i.e. from the initial stage of receipt
of application to the final stage of sanction or rejection, as the case may be. The issue concerning exemption
of stamp duty on land mortgage comes under the purview of respective State Governments, as ‘mortgage’
falls in the State List under the Constitution of India. SIDBI generally creates mortgage by deposit of title
deeds as a security for providing the financial assistance to SSI units. Mortgage by deposit of title deeds does
not attract any stamp duty in the Union Territory of Delhi. In Noida and Ghaziabad, which fall in the State of
Uttar Pradesh, stamp duty @ ½ per cent of the amount secured subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,000/- is
payable in such cases.
          (ii)     As explained above, the stamp duty on land mortgage is a State subject. Similarly, administrative changes
to ease the process of registration and payment of stamp duties also fall within the domain of the State
Governments.
          (iii)    The Government in consultation with Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has formulated
a financial package for State Financial Corporations (SFCs). According to this package, SIDBI will provide
the following reliefs and concessions to SFCs:----                                                               
                      (a)    Interest on all outstanding loans of SFCs will be reduced by 2 per cent;
                      (b)    A rebate of 2 per cent in the rate of interest will be provided by SIDBI for all future refinance; and
                      (c)    A moratorium of one year shall be given for repayment of existing dues. The effective
implementation of these reliefs and concessions necessitate commensurate measures by State
Governments and SFCs. The package entails signing of MOUs by the State Government and SFCs
with SIDBI. It is expected that the above restructuring of the refinance portfolio of SIDBI for SFCs
would improve their viability and enable them to meet the needs of SSI sector.
2.2     Study the viability of SSI Bank Units
2.2.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee is of the opinion that there is a strong need for a mechanism which could study the viability of

SSI units. The Committee suggests that an independent agency needs to be set up. This agency should also make
available the credit rating of the SSIs. The Committee therefore, directs the Ministry of SSI to look into this issue and
take necessary steps.(Para 5.5)
2.2.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The Group of Ministers on SSI had decided that RBI should draw up revised, detailed, transparent and non-
discretionary guidelines for the rehabilitation of sick and potentially viable SSI units. Accordingly, the RBI constituted a
Working Group under the Chairmanship of Shri S.S. Kohli, the then Chairman of IBA. Based on the recommendations
of the Working Group, the RBI issued revised guidelines for the rehabilitation of sick and potentially viable SSI units on
16th January, 2002. The revised guidelines contain suitable measures to study viability of SSI unit by the individual
financing banks. As regards credit rating of the SSIs, Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has been
working on a suitable model. The National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) is also working on a Rating Scheme for
Small Industries to be implemented through them.
2.3     Tax Relief on Income of individuals
2.3.1  Observation/Recommendation
          In order to boost the credit flow, the Committee feels that the Government should consider the tax relief on
income of individuals who make an investment in SSIs in the form of deposit in those units.                              (Para 5.6)
2.3.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The Ministry of Finance has undertaken reform in Direct Taxation over the last decade. The general direction of
these reforms is towards reducing the deductions/exemptions and thereby reducing general tax rates. Accordingly, new
tax concessions are not contemplated. However, the Income-tax Act already provides for a variety of fiscal incentives
for industrial activity, including SSIs. These concessions include a tax holiday for Undertakings set up in Backward
States and Districts, a tax holiday for Undertakings set up in certain special category States such as the North­-Eastern
States and Himachal Pradesh and Uttaranchal, a tax holiday for Undertakings engaged in the business of operating cold
chain and storage facilities, marketing and handling of Food grains, a Tax holiday for units in Special Economic Zones
and 100 per cent Export Oriented Units, etc. In addition, loans to SSI already get a preferential treatment over equity as
unlike dividends, interest payable by SSIs on Deposits made with it is fully allowable as a Tax-deductible expense in the
bands of the SSI.
2.4     Tax Exemptions
2.4.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee further tells that tax exemptions may be allowed up to Rs. 2 lakhs with a view to motivate them to
show profits in their balance sheets and have enough cash flow to pay instalments of loans or upgrade the plant and
machinery. After 2 lakhs, there should be slabs of 10 per cent, 20 per cent and 25 per cent as corporate tax. This will
certainly give strength to SSI units to meet the challenges of the competitive
market.                                                              (Para 5.8)
2.4.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) have informed that stability of Tax rates has been one of the corner-
stones of Government’s Tax policy. Raising of Taxable limit would not be possible, as it would skew the Tax-rate
structure. The Income-tax Act already provides for a variety of fiscal incentives for Small Scale Industries.
2.5     Recognition and Awards
2.5.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee also recommends that the Industrial Area Manufacturers Associations, in the respective Industrial
areas should be involved to provide inputs regarding outstanding branches/officers for recognition and awards to
individual branches and or individual officers in the branches.
                                                                                                                                                  (Para 5.11)
2.5.2  Action Taken/Comments
          As regards the recommendation of the Committee that the Industrial Area Manufacturers Associations should be
involved to provide inputs regarding outstanding branches/officers for recognition and awards to individual
branches/officers, the RBI is of the view that it may not be appropriate to introduce such rewarding systems depending

2.6     Ground of rejection of Loan Application
2.6.1  Observation/Recommendation
          As regards the rejection, the Committee recommends that if any proposal from SSI Sector is rejected, or not
entertained by any Bank Manager then
          (i)     the applicant should be informed in writing of the reasons for rejection and also the suggestions for
submission of the complete and valid application;
          (ii)     the rejection decision should be ratified by the next higher authority at the Zonal/Regional office.
                                                                                                                                                    (Para 5.12)
2.6.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The RBI has informed that instructions already exist in this regard which are reiterated to the banks from time to
time.
2.7     Proper Bankruptcy Laws
2.7.1  Observation/Recommendation
          In India, there are no proper bankruptcy laws. The process of restructuring and winding of companies is totally
ineffective and counterproductive. By the time, enterprises are declared sick, it is too late for restructuring. The
enterprise promoters get enough time to tunnel out all the assets leaving workers and creditors high and dry. In view of
the present situation, the Committee strongly recommends that a comprehensive bankruptcy law should be enacted
under which if an enterprise misses a payment exceeding hundred thousand rupees, creditors are given the right to take
legal action leading to the filing of bankruptcy by the enterprise. This process will shorten the bureaucratic procedures,
and therefore, provide better protection to workers and
creditors.                                                                                             (Para 5.15)
2.7.2  Action Taken/Comments
          Based on the recommendations of the Committee constituted under the Chairmanship of Justice V. Balakrishan
Eradi (Eradi Committee), Companies Act, 1956 has been amended through Companies (Second Amendment) Act, 2003
with the main objective of facilitating or expediting revival/rehabilitation of sick companies and protection of workers
interests/dues of creditors and where necessary, winding up of companies. Further, Sick Industrial Companies (Special
Provisions) Repeal Act, 2004 has also been passed by the Parliament.
2.8     Modernization Package for Powerlooms
2.8.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Finance Minister in his Budget speech on the Finance Bill, 2003 stated that “The Government wanted to
totally protect the interest of the small and the self employed weavers and garment manufacturers. The Government had
announced a modernization package for powerlooms. The Government had also announced a financial and technical
package for the modernization of the entire textile industry like the Government had done it for the steel industry”. The
Government also propose to fully exempt from excise duty for unbranded woven and knitted readymade garments upto
the first level of Rs. 25 lakh provided that the annual turnover does not exceed Rs. 30 lakh. Almost 85 per cent of the
garment manufacturers are in this Rs. 20.00 lakh to Rs. 25.00 lakh bracket. Therefore, the Committee is of the view that
this exemption scheme should be extended to garments of rubberized textile fabrics, cotton benching, mosquito nets and
fabrics of mono-filarment.           (Para 5.16)
2.8.2  Action Taken/Comments
          Vide Notification No. 36/2003-CE, dated 30.04.2003, (i) fabrics of monofilament, (ii) rubberized textile fabrics,
and (iii) woven and unprocessed cotton belting, have already been exempted from central excise duty for the first annual
clearance of Rs. 25 lakhs provided that the annual turnover does not exceed Rs. 35 lakh. Vide Notification No. 70/2003-
CE, dated 04.09.2003, mosquito net fabrics have been unconditionally exempted from the whole of the central excise
duty. Further, mosquito nets is covered under the General SSI Excise Exemption Scheme (Notifications No. 8/2003-CE
and No. 9/2003-CE, both dated 1.3.2003).

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT
ACCEPTED THE REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT
3.1     Time Limit for Declaring a SSI Units as a Non Performance
3.1.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee is of the opinion that the time limit for declaring a SSI unit as a non performance assets should be
increased taking into consideration the various factors such as delayed payments, blockage of credit flow, corruption,
enactment of Securitization Act etc. which are hindering the growth of small scale industries.            (Para 5.2)
3.1.2  Action Taken/Comments
          In line with the international practices and as per the recommendations made by the Committee on the Financial
System under the Chairmanship of Shri M. Narasimham, the Reserve Bank of India has introduced, in a phased manner,
prudential norms for income recognition, asset classification and provisioning for the advances portfolio of the banks so
as to move towards greater consistency and transparency in the public accounts. The policy of income recognition has to
be objective and based on record of recovery rather than on any subjective considerations. Likewise, the classification of
assets of banks has to be done on the basis of objective criteria, which would ensure a uniform and consistent
application of the norms. Furthermore, the provisioning needs to be made on the basis of the classification of assets
based on the period for which the asset has remained non-performing and the availability of security and the realizable
value thereof.
3.1.3  Further Recommendation
          The Committee appreciates the recommendations of the Committee on Financial System for prudential norms for
income reorganization, assets classification and provisioning for advances portfolio of banks are necessary for greater
consistency and transparency. As the provisioning needs to be made on the basis of classification of assets, the
Committee would like to be apprised of the criteria for prudential norms for income recognition and assest
classification. The Ministry should therefore clarify before the Committee the specific criteria set out to implement the
said norms.
3.2     State of Art Technology Changes
3.2.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The age when technology becomes rapidly obsolete, the cost of making state of art technology changes and of
pioneering areas with the inbuilt axiom, high risk, high return, the Committee observes that the assistance under venture
capital funds has assumed unprecedented importance. Just as the SIDBI’s National Venture Fund for development of
SSIs in software/IT industry in collaboration with Ministry of Information Technology and Government of India and the
Technology Development and Modernisation Fund (TDMF), there should be special Scheme in order to assist SSIs in
other areas. The Committee feels that the Commercial Banks should come forward in launching venture capital funds in
all its ramifications so as to effectively integrate and enhance the opportunities for Small Scale Industries in domestic
and International market. The banks should endeavour to set up more and more venture capital fund not only in
software/IT industry but also for high growth sectors such as bio-technology and food processing inter-alia.  The
Committee feels that Government should come forward to set up Technology Upgradation and Development Banks to
take stock of ground realities of sickness of SSI units due to obsolescence of technology and assist the units by ensuring
credit facilitation at appropriate time and thus save the sick but potentially viable SSI units before dying
out.                                                                                    (Para 5.3)
3.2.2  Action Taken/Comments
          To encourage Venture Capital funding to SSI units, the banks have been advised by the RBI that investment in
venture capital will be eligible for inclusion in priority sector lending. This is subject to the condition that the venture
capital funds/companies are registered with Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Further, in the recently held
meeting of the RBI’s Standing Advisory Committee on flow of institutional credit to SSI on 1st September, 2003, one of
the action points that emerged was that the banks should initiate innovative steps for increasing credit flow by means of
promoting Mutual Funds to SSI and venture capital funds, which has been communicated to all banks.
3.2.3  SIDB1 has so far promoted/contributed to 6 all India and 9 Regional Funds. Of these, 9 are IT and Software
dedicated, one is for the auto ancillary sector and 5 are general funds. Canbank Venture Capital Fund III has been set up
in collaboration with Canara Bank on equal sharing basis. Certain commercial banks have also joined hands with SIDBI

in promoting APIDC Venture Capital Fund (Andhra Bank and Indian Overseas Bank), Auto Ancillary Fund (UCO
Bank), SARA Fund (Punjab & Sind Bank and ICICI Bank) and SICOM Venture Capital Fund (Ratnakar Bank Ltd. and
United Western Bank Ltd.). Apart from the above, SIDBI has agreed in-principle to contribute Rs.25 crore to the corpus
of SEAF India SME Fund. SIDBI has also agreed to contribute Rs.5 crore for setting up Micro Ventures Innovation
Fund in collaboration with National Innovation Foundation, Ahmedabad. As on date, SIDBI’s aggregate commitments
to the Venture Capital Funds is Rs. 150.13 crore and aggregate disbursements to the tune of Rs 83.36 crore.
3.2.4  SIDBI constituted an in-house team of officials in October, 2000 to look into the modalities of setting up of a
Technology Bank for the SSI. The in-house team submitted its report in March, 2001 on the possible framework of the
proposed Technology Bank. The report was tabled before the Board of Directors of SIDBI, which considered the report
and opined that the matter needed independent study by a reputed consultant. The study has been completed in June
2003 and the consultants have submitted their report, which is being analysed by SIDBI. Based on the report and the
road map outlined by the consultants, further action is being initiated for setting up the Technology Bank.
3.2.5  Further Recommendation
          The Committee observes that assistance under Venture Capital Fund has gained importance and the banks
accordingly have been advised by RBI that investment in the Venture Capital would be eligible for inclusion in priority
sector lending. The contribution made by SIDBI is certainly noteworthy. The Committee gathers an impression that
certain commercial banks are still approaching the SIDBI to join hands in promoting Venture Capital Funds.
          The Committee also takes note of number of funds set up by various banks at all India and regional level. The
Committee appreciates the progress made so far in this regard and feels that a lot more is yet to be done to reach the
desired level. The Committee observes that about half of the aggregate commitments of Venture Capital Funds could be
disbursed so far. The Committee would like to know the reasons for under utilization and also measures taken or being
taken by banks and funding agencies to promote the same. The Committee may also be apprised of the progress being
made by other banks and funding agencies which are, yet, to set up Venture Capital Funds.
          As regards the setting up of Technology Bank for the SSIs the Committee notes from the reply that the study has
already been completed and report is still being analyzed by SIDBI. The Committee feels that about three years have
been taken by the SIDBI since setting up of its In-house Committee for working out the modalities and road map is still
not cleared. The Committee conveys its concern over the delay in this regard. The Committee therefore directs the
Government and the SIDBI to expedite the setting up technology banks as soon as possible.
3.3     Industry Oriented Branches
3.3.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The increased competition has improved the working of various banks. This should be encouraged by opening
more industry oriented branches in the approved industrial areas. The Reserve Bank of India should be requested to
grant more licenses to banks for opening branches in the Industrial areas.
                                                                                                                                                    (Para 5.10)
3.3.2  Action Taken/Comments
          Banks are free to open Specialised Industrial Finance and SSI branches without RBI approval. They are only
required to obtain their Board’s approval and a licence from concerned Regional Office of RBI before opening the
branch to comply with Section 23 of Banking Regulation Act, 1949. As on 31st March, 2003, the specialised SSI bank
branches have increased to 417 in the country.
3.3.3  Further Recommendation
          Though banks are opening the SSI branches under the guidance and instructions issued by the concerned
Regional Office of RBI and their Board is approved, yet the Committee desires to know the updated position of
SSI branches as on 31st March, 2004.
3.4     Linkage between Term Loans and Working Capital
3.4.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee also feels that another fact calling for attention is the need to provide a linkage between term
loans and working capital so that there is no duplicity in agencies providing it and thus saving the SSIs from caprice of
multiple sanctions. The narrow access to banks finance due to cumbersome procedure and the exhaustive regulations
prescribed by the bank warrant that the prevailing narrow access to bank finance affecting the productivity of units
engaged in SSI activities be made adequate and
conducive.                                                                                                              (Para 5.14)

3.4.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The coordination between SFCs and banks in sanctioning the term loans and working capital facilities
respectively to an SSI unit is found to be a major problem faced by the units. This often results in units, which are ready
for production after availing the term loan from the SFCs, have to wait for the bank’s clearance on working capital. This
problem of SSI units is likely to be solved to a great extent by the enhancement of the composite loan limit to Rs. 50
lakh, which would enable majority of units to avail both the term loan and working capital from a Single Window.
3.4.3  Under the refinance window, SIDBI is operating the Single Window Scheme for providing term loan and working
capital through the same agency. The scheme is being operated through SFCs and banks.
3.4.4  Further Recommendation
          Though the Committee feels that lack of coordination between SFCs and banks in sanctioning the terms loans and
working capital facilities to SSI unit is a major problem faced by the units which could hopefully be solved by
enhancing the composite loan limit to Rs.50 lakh. The Committee direct the Ministry to furnish the details of its Single
Window Scheme.

4.1     Delayed Payment Act
4.1.1  Observation/Recommendation
          The Committee also recommends that Delayed Payment Act should be given teeth to control and punish
organizations holding and delaying payments to SSI. Under the present Act, the facilitation committee should be a sub-
committee nominated by the Divisional Udyog Bandhu having full powers to arbitrate under the provisions of
arbitration act.(Para 5.7)
4.1.2  Action Taken/Comments
          The Government enacted Interest on Delayed Payments to Small Scale and Ancillary Industrial Undertakings Act
in 1993. However, the problem of delay in payment of bills for supplies made by Small Scale Industrial (SSI) units to
large industries continued despite enactment of a separate law. The Act was therefore, amended in 1998. In the amended
Act, the State Governments have been given an active role in the implementation of the provisions of the law with a
view to providing speedy relief to the SSI suppliers. The most important change that has been brought about by the
amendment Act is that the SSI suppliers can now approach the Industry Facilitation Councils (IFCs) for settlement of
their disputes with the buyers in regard to delay in payment etc. of the supplies made by them.
4.1.3  Representations were received from Industrial Associations for making the provisions of the Act more effective
so that necessary relief could be expeditiously provided to the SSI units. After holding consultations with Industrial
Associations and considering various recommendations received on amendments to the Delayed Payment Act, 1993, a
draft Cabinet Note is under circulation to the concerned Ministries/Departments for their comments.

          REPORT
          The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries on the
Recommendations contained in the 130th Report (of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Industry) on the Credit Flow to SSI Sector in Himachal Pradesh pertaining to the Ministry of Small Scale Industries.
The Report was presented/laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha on the on 22nd December, 2003.
2.       Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Small Scale Industries in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:---
Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries: (Chapter-
I)
Recommendations : 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.10, 2.11, 2.18, 2.36, 2 37, 2.48, 3.44, 3.48, 3.50, 4.19, 4.23, 4.25, 4.27
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government’s
replies: (Chapter-II)
Recommendations : 3.3, 3.16, 3.22, 3.38, 3.46, 3.52
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies of the Ministry:
(Chapter-III)
Recommendations : 2.39, 3.5, 3.7, 3.27, 3.30, 3.39, 3.40, 3.41, 3.42, 3.43
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry have not been received:
(Chapter-IV)
Recommendations : 2.41, 3.9, 3.24, 4.3, 4.16, 4.29
3.       The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendation as mentioned in Chapter-
I of the Report.
4.       In respect of the recommendations made in Chapter-II the Committee is convinced with the logic and explanation
advocated by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue further.
5.       The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendations contained in Chapter-III
and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanation in respect of these recommendations.
6.       In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished the interim replies or
couched its language in vague terms like noted for compliance/guidance, therefore, the Committee directs that the
Ministry should furnish Action Taken “Notes in respects of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to
the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
7.       The Details of the ATR is being discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
Recommendation
1.1     Pattern of industrialization in Himachal Pradesh
1.1.1 The Committee feels that industrialization in Himachal Pradesh has been concentrated around few districts and a
large area of the State remains unaffected by industrialization. The Committee strongly recommends that new areas be
developed and the process of industrialization spread in a manner so as to benefit the State as a whole.            
                                                                                                                                            (Para: 2.7)
Action Taken
1.1.2  The State Government has informed that the entire State of Himachal Pradesh is industrially backward except

155th Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/155threport.htm[04-07-2016 12:51:24]
some development on the periphery of the State. In the Industrial Policy 1999, the State has been classified into two
categories namely “Industrially developing areas” and “Industrially backward areas”. Tribal areas of the State, as
notified from time to time have been treated as tax-free industrial zones to promote industrial development in these
areas. To encourage industrial development in the interior areas, which are also industrially backward areas, graded
incentives have been provided in the Industrial Policy.
1.1.3  In order to ensure equitable industrial development, the Department of Industries has so far developed 31
industrial areas and 11 industrial estates in the State. Besides, the Department has in its possession few undeveloped
patches of land at certain locations. More Government land is being identified for creating a Land Bank which could be
utilized for the establishment of new industries. This would further help in the equitable industrial development of the
State.
Recommendation
1.2     Human resource development facilities
1.2.1  The Committee observed that human resource development facilities particularly in vocational and technical
education are not adequate in Himachal Pradesh. The Committee recommends that the local industry and State
Government should join hands to restructure training programmes so as to provide employment to the youth.
                                                                                                                                            (Para: 2.8)
Action Taken
1.2.3  The local industry and the State Government have recommended several areas in which the Industrial Training
Institutes (ITIs) and the industry could cooperate. One such area relates to restructuring of training programmes at the
ITIs by providing more autonomy to the Institutes through decentralization and to make training accountable to users.
For this purpose; it was proposed to constitute a High Powered Committee for each ITI for carrying on the suggested
activities effectively.
1.2.4  It was decided to take up one ITI in each district as pilot project. Based on the experience gained from the
cooperation other ITIs could be taken up later. Accordingly, it was proposed to constitute a separate Institute Managing
Committee (IMC) for each III having representation of State Government, Industry and others. It was also proposed to
constitute a Steering Committee at the State level under the Chairmanship of Stale Secretary Incharge of Vocational
Training which would decide the powers to be devolved to the IMCs, their functions and monitor and evaluate their
performance. To begin with, it was decided to take up one ITI as pilot project under the Scheme and ITI Solan was
selected as the Pilot Project in consultation with CII.
1.2.5  Based on the success achieved in the implementation of Pilot Project at ITT Solan, all the ITIs in the State are to
be covered in a phased manner under the scheme The IMCs for the ITIs at Nalagarh, Paunta Sahib, Nahan, Una,
Chamba, Shapur, Nehranpukhar, Nadaun, Bilaspur, Mandi, Rampur, Shamshi (W), Dharamshala and Sundernagar (PH)
have been constituted and notified by the Government. The meeting of the IMCs are being held at regular intervals with
the active participation of CII and the industries located in the areas. The proposal for the constitution of IMCs for the
rest of ITIs (except ITI Reckong Peo and Shimla) have been sent to the Government for notification, as has been
suggested by the Principals of respective ITIs. The primary objective of the scheme is to increase the relevance of the
training programmes conducted at the ITIs.
Recommendation
1.3     Incentives in industrially backward areas
1.3.1 The Committee observed that the entire State is industrially backward except some development on the periphery
of the State. The Committee feels that there is a need to give over-riding incentives in industrially backward areas. A
special package of incentives is required for fruit, vegetable and maize based units consuming locally available raw
material. In addition, emphasis is also to be given to thrust areas including 100% EOU’s For the units in large and
medium scale sector more emphasis is required to be laid for providing better infrastructure. In order to accelerate and
facilitate industrialization, clearances required for setting up of units in industrially developed areas shall be specially
dealt on fast track basis. The Committee also observed that Income Tax holiday and that Central Transport Subsidy
Scheme, the two major central incentives have helped the growth of industries in the State. The Committee also felt that
the Government of India should be approached to extend these incentives.
                                                                                                                                          (Para: 2.9)
Action Taken
1.3.2  The Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion has announced a new Industrial Policy and other concessions to

155th Report of Committee on Industry

promote industrialisation in the State of Himachal Pradesh on 7th January, 2003. Graded incentives have been provided
in the Industrial Policy to encourage industrial development in the interior areas. Tribal areas of the State, as notified
from time to time, have been made as tax-free industrial zones to promote industrial development in these areas. Priority
sector industries have been identified and
special incentives are admissible for the setting up of fruit, vegetable and maize based units. In addition, Government of
India is also providing special incentives to such units. The details of the incentives provided by the State Government
and the Central Government to Food Processing Industries are given below:----
State Government Incentives

per the provision made under incentive rules - 1999.
