THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT
ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT
Recommendation
3.0    Fiscal/Financial Incentives for New Technologies/Modernization
3.1 The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry to make the SSIs to meet the global standards,
however, the Committee is of the view that to tackle the paradoxical situation of upgradation of technology and at the
same time fund constraints in the SSI sector the Government must consider subsidizing the cost of upgradation by way
of fiscal/financial incentives to help SSI for the adoption of new technologies/ modernization. Further the Ministry
should initiate the opening of technology exchanges for providing necessary information on technology and bench
marking the international quality standards, so as to integrate domestic markets with the international markets.
Knowledge networking through linkage of research institutes with the SSI sector would be effective too for integration
of the sector with the broader markets.          (Para 53)
Action Taken
3.1.1The Ministry of SSI has launched the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation of the
SSIs (CLCSS). The scheme provides 12 per cent capital subsidy on institutional finance with the eligible loan ceiling of
Rs. 40 lakh, for induction of well-established and improved technology in the specified products/sub-sectors. It is now
proposed to enhance the subsidy to 15 per cent and the ceiling of the loan eligible for support to Rs. 1 crore, as
announced in the Union Budget for 2004-05.
3.1.2Technology Resource Centres (TRCs) have been set up in all Small Industries Service Institutes having facilities of
networking with leading organizations engaged in technology upgradation so that SSI units can access the appropriate
technologies and attain international standards. The TRCs have collection of technical books, catalogues, brochures,
etc., in addition to providing information on “How to seek technology”, technology transfer mode, leading technology
transfer agencies, international exhibitions, etc. Web links have been given from SIDO Portal (www.laghu-udyog.com)
to SIDBI, dedicated branches of commercial banks, all State Government Industries Departments, etc. On-line
networking has also been provided to technology database hosted on www.techsmall.com by Technology Bureau for
Small Enterprises (TBSE).
Further Recommendation
3.1.3The Committee is of the considered view that with the opening up of national economy, there is the need for
consolidation of domestic SSI sector to enable the SSI units to face the stiff competition with the global SSI products. In
this regard, reduction in the cost of production through introduction of latest technology and knowledge networking
through linkages of research institute with the SSI sector becomes all the more necessary. The Committee welcomes the
setting up of Technology Resource Centres (TRCs) and hopes that its promotional role would prove significant for
integration of the SSI sector with the global market. The Committee however be informed of the impact of these
incentives in SSI sector and the monitoring mechanism for implementation.
Recommendation

3.2    Impact of Globalization and Liberalization on Small Scale Sector and Role of Banks
3.2.1The Committee takes note of the information provided by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries regarding impact
of Globalization and Liberalization on Small Scale Sector and role of banks. The Committee appreciates that
considering the funds constraints with SSI sector, the Government has introduced the credit linked capital subsidy
scheme for Technology upgradation of Small Scale Industries under which 12% back ended capital subsidy would be
admissible on the loans advanced to the SSIs by the scheduled commercial banks/designated State Financial
Corporations for technology upgradation in certain select sectors. The Committee understands that a Study Group on
development of Small Scale Enterprises made a number of recommendations like setting up of a Technology Bank,
providing of finance to units for entering into collaboration for technical know-how and technology upgradation etc.
The Committee therefore recommends that these recommendations of the study group should be implemented in true
spirit to support SSI Sector. Having taken note of the fact that only a small number of entrepreneurs took the advantage
of the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme. The Committee feels that many more entrepreneurs could be benefited if
a wide publicity is given to Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme. The Committee therefore, calls upon the
Government to accord due publicity to this scheme and be handed over to the State Governments for
implementation.                                                                                                                (Para 54)
Action Taken
3.2.2SIDBI had set up the Technology Bureau for Small Enterprises (TBSE) in 1995 to help SMEs tap opportunities at
the global level for acquisition of technology and establish business collaborations. TBSE has taken several initiatives
and put in place an effective mechanism to address the technology and collaboration related needs of the sector. TBSE
has set up a technology site for small industries at www.techsmall.com. Its endeavor is to provide information on
technology at the doorstep of user enterprises. Recognizing the contribution of TBSE, it was indicated in the
Comprehensive Policy Package for SSI that TBSE will be strengthened so that it functions effectively as a Technology
Bank. SIDBI has initiated necessary steps for institutionalizing TBSE as a full-fledged Technology Bank.
3.2.3SIDBI has also taken several steps for popularizing the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology
Upgradation of the SSIs (CLCSS).
3.2.4The operation of CLCSS is being reviewed at the meetings of the State Level Bankers Committee. All Primary
Lending Institutions (PLIs) have been advised to conduct workshops, seminars and conferences to popularize the
Scheme. They have also been advised to circulate the details of the Scheme at meetings and seminars organized by
Industry Associations, State Governments, etc. Some Industry Associations have covered the Scheme in their periodic
bulletin for disseminating information among their members. The Scheme has also been covered in the Journal of the
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. All District Industries Centres/ various Industry Associations have been
provided details of the Scheme, requesting them to circulate it among the industries. Staff Training Centres of banks
have been forwarded copy of the Scheme. Awareness sessions on CLCSS are also being conducted in Bankers Training
Colleges. Interactive sessions inviting bankers and entrepreneurs have been held in various potential Centres/clusters.
3.2.5The Scheme is being publicised by SIDBI and the Office of the DC (SSI) among SSI units, by organizing
awareness programmes. The guidelines of the Scheme have been posted on SIDO’s website. Revised guidelines have
been printed and circulated to all SISIs, PLIs, SIDBI, NABARD, Industry Associations, State Secretaries/Directors of
Industries, etc.
3.2.6CLCSS is a specialized scheme under which subsidy is provided for well-­established and improved technologies
for the select products/sub-sectors. For identification of improved technologies, expert institutions in the respective
fields are consulted and technologies are approved by a Technical Sub-Committee under the chairmanship of the DC
(SSI). The Scheme is being implemented at the national level through two nodal agencies, viz., SIDBI and NABARD
through Primary Lending Institutions (i.e., Banks, SFCs, Cooperative lending institutions). SIDBI and NABARD are,
however, national agencies. It would thus be difficult for them to deal with individual State Governments to run the
Scheme. Therefore, it is not administratively feasible to hand over the operation of the Scheme to State Governments.
Further Recommendation
3.2.7Although SIDBI had set up the Technology Bureau for Small Enterprises (TBSE) in 1995 to help SMEs tap
opportunities at the global level for acquisition of technology and establish business collaborations, however, nothing
substantial has come out in regard to fulfilment of technology and collaboration related needs of the sector. The
Committee therefore, recommends that SIDBI should make action plan for popularization of the function aspects of
Technology Bureau for Small Enterprises (TBSE). Besides there is the need for further popularization of Credit Linked

Capital Subsidy Scheme and development mechanism for appropriate addressing the technological requirement for SSI
sector.
Recommendation
3.3    Corpus for Credit Guarantee Fund Trust Scheme for Small Industries (CGTSI)
3.3.1There has been demand to increase the corpus for Credit Guarantee Fund Trust Scheme for Small Industries
(CGTSI). The Committee is of the view that the demand for raising the existing corpus for CGTSI should be
sympathetically considered by the Government. The Committee feels that coverage under the scheme needs to be
extended. The Committee further impress upon the Government to pursue with RBI to ensure that all the private sector
Banks and foreign Banks are involved in lending to SSI units. In addition, the banks may open more branches specially
for lending to SSIs.(Para 55)
Action Taken
3.3.2The Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small Industries was launched in August, 2000 to mitigate the problems of
collateral security and third party guarantee faced by the SSI/tiny units in accessing credit facilities of the banking
system. The Government of India (GoI) and SIDBI contribute to the Corpus Fund of the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust
for Small Industries (CGTSI), operating the Credit Guarantee Scheme, in the ratio of 4:1. In order to increase the
comfort level of the Member Banks/Lending Institutions (MLIs) and encourage them to extend more collateral-free
credit facilities to the SSIs/SSSBEs under the Credit Guarantee Scheme, it is necessary to build the Corpus Fund of the
Trust. Taking into account the progress under the Scheme, the initial corpus of the Trust of Rs. 125 crore has been
gradually enhanced with contribution by the GoI and SIDBI. As at the end of September, 2004, the corpus fund under
the Scheme was Rs. 767.44 crore, with contribution of Rs. 613.95 crore from the GoI (including Rs. 65 crore released
from the budget provision for the Scheme during FY 2004-05) and Rs. 153.49 crore from SIDBI. During FY 2004-05, a
provision of Rs. 196.29 crore was made in the Budget Estimates, which is proposed to be enhanced at the Revised
Estimate stage. The proposed enhancement of the Corpus Fund is intended to achieve higher coverage of SSI/tiny units
under the Scheme.
3.3.3The scope of the Credit Guarantee Scheme has been widened. Effective from 1
st September, 2003, credit facilities
upto Rs. 25 lakh, sanctioned without collateral security and/or third party guarantee by the MLIs to the new and existing
Small Scale Service and Business (Industry Related) Enterprises (SSSBEs) have also been made eligible for coverage
under the Scheme. On account of the continuous efforts made by CGTSI to create greater awareness about the Credit
Guarantee Scheme, there has been a distinct improvement in the awareness levels among the MLIs and the SSI
entrepreneurs, which is reflected in the increased coverage by MLIs under the Scheme. As on 30
th September, 2004,
18,720 proposals involving credit of Rs. 333.87 crore have been approved under Credit Guarantee Scheme. So far, 50
banks/lending institutions (27 Public Sector Banks, 12 Private Sector Banks, 8 Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and 3
Institutions, viz., NSIC, NEDFI and SIDBI) have registered as MLIs of CGTSI. CGTSI has been making efforts to enlist
the remaining private sector banks, foreign banks, as also eligible RRBs as MLIs to participate in the Credit Guarantee
Scheme.
3.3.4Lending to Small Scale Industries is included under priority sector lending obligations by banks under the target of
40 per cent of Net Bank Credit laid down in this regard. The RBI guidelines on flow of credit to the SSI sector are
issued to all Scheduled Commercial Banks (which include public, private and foreign banks). For foreign banks within
the overall target of 32% of priority sector lending to be achieved, the advances to the SSI sector should not be less than
10% of the Net Bank Credit. Foreign banks failing to achieve lending target to priority sector or sub-target (within the
priority sector) are required to deposit the shortfall amount with SIDBI. SIDBI utilizes these deposits for extending
refinance to banks/ FIs, which have extended finance to the SSI sector.
3.3.5Banks have also been advised to open at least one Specialized SSI branch in each District. Funther, banks have
been permitted to categories their general banking branches having 60% or more of their advances to the SSI sector as
Specialized SSI branches, in order to provide better service to this sector as a whole. As on 3lst March, 2004, the public
sector banks have 497 Specialized SSI branches all over the country.
Further Recommendation
3.3.6 The Committee is of the considered view that the enhancement of the corpus for Credit Guarantee Fund Trust
Scheme for Small Industries (CGTSI) would lead to larger coverage of collateral free and without third party guarantee

has gradually been enhanced to Rs. 767.44 crore in September, 2004 but the quantum of corpus is not adequate yet,
therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Government should suitable enhance the corpus fund to increase

3.4    Delay in Implementation of Nayak Committee recommendations
3.4.1The Committee was informed of the delay in implementation of Nayak Committee recommendations especially
with regard to the working capital as 20% of the projected turnover and strengthening of State Level Inter-Institutional
Committees (SLIICs) on the lines of the erstwhile BIFR for SSI units. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Government should come forward to help the SSI sector in acquiring working capital at the rate of 20% of their projects
turnover. As regards setting up of the SLIICs, the Committee is of the view that the Government should speed up the
action on the recommendation so as to revive the sick and sinking SSI units in the country.                                              
(Para 57)
Action Taken
3.4.2Based on Nayak Committee recommendations, banks have been advised by the RBI to compute the working
capital requirement of SSI units, on the basis of the simplified method of minimum 20% of the projected annual
turnover of the borrowing unit for limits up to Rs.5 crore. Instructions in this regard have been reiterated from time to
time.
3.4.3To address the issue of sickness of SSI units and their rehabilitation, State Level Inter-Institutional Committee
(SLIIC) has been set up in each State under the chairmanship of the Secretary, Industries Department of the State
concerned. The SLIIC deals with the problems of co-ordination in rehabilitation of sick SSI units. The meetings are
generally held quarterly. A Sub-Committee of SLIIC has also been set up in every State to discuss rehabilitation of
individual units in the presence of the borrower and the bank concerned.
Further Recommendation
3.4.4 The Committee reiterates the implementation of Nayak Committee’s recommendation in competition of working
capital requirement of SSI units on the basis of the simplified method of minimum of 20 % of projected annual turn over
of the borrowing units. The Committee desires that State Level Inter Institutional Committee (SLIIC) should improve
upon its functional aspects and come out with sustainable strategy for re-habilitation of sick SSI units.
Recommendation
3.5    Insistence of collateral securities by various banks
3.5.1The Committee takes a serious view on the issue of insistence of collateral securities by various banks and also to
the non-displaying of the details in their branches that the collateral free loans are available to the SSI units. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should direct all the banks not to insist for collateral securities
and to display the details of availability of collateral free loans.                                                                       (Para 59)
Action Taken
3.5.2To improve the flow of credit to the SSI sector, the RBI advised the banks in January, 2002 to dispense with the
collateral security requirement for loans upto Rs. 5 lakh to all SSI units. Further, in April, 2002 the RBI advised the
banks that they may, on the basis of good track record and financial position of the units, increase the limit of loan, for
dispensing with the collateral security requirement, from the existing Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 15 lakh (enhanced to Rs.25 lakh
as per announcement made in the Mid-Term Review of the Monetary and Credit Policy 2003-04). For loans covered
under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small Industries, collateral securities are not required upto the borrowing
limit of Rs.25 lakh. The RBI has informed that on receipt of specific complaints against any bank, the matter is
investigated and necessary remedial action initiated accordingly.
3.5.3The RBI has advised the banks to initiate necessary steps to give adequate publicity to their schemes/facilities, like
availability of collateral-free /composite loan and schemes under TUFs/NEFlKVIC/CGTSI, etc. As informed by the
RBI, almost all the public sector banks have initiated steps to implement these instructions. Further, to increase

was advertised in all leading newspapers. Indian Banks Association (IBA) has issued a circular to all member banks to
come out with similar charter for SSI sector. All 27 public sector banks have issued Charter for SSI . CGTSI has also
been taking necessary steps to publicize the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small Industries.
Further Recommendation
3.5.4The Committee desires to communicate the resentment and anguish of SSI Associations that despite the repeated
guidelines of Reserve Bank of India to the Public Sector Banks for lending collateral free and without third party
guarantee a loan up to a limit of Rs. 25 lakh, the Public Sector Banks do not abide by the guidelines of Reserve Bank of
India. The general experience is that banks insist on collateral securities and mortgages for lending credit even for lower
amount of money. It is further stated that banks are not providing SSI friendly working atmosphere as the bankers point
out larger incidence of sickness in the SSI sector. In the meeting of Sub-Committee-II for the Ministry of Small Scale
Industries (of Standing Committee on Industry) held on 11
th April, 2005, the SSI Associations raised issues even against
SIDBI which is not providing desirable services to the SSI units. The Committee therefore, recommends that bankers
have to change their mind set and assist the SSI units in extending credit as per their requirement as SSI sector has the
potential for employment generation and consolidation of national economy.

4.0    Limit of 120 days for payment to SSI units be brought down to 30 days
4.1    The Committee takes note of the demand of SSI Associations that the limit of 120 days for payment to SSI units
be brought down to 30 days and recommends that the Government should speed up the necessary action to complete the
mandatory requirement to amend the relevant Delayed Payments to Small Scale and Associations Industrial
Undertakings Act, 1998.                                                                                                                               (Para 58)
Action Taken
4.1.1Amendment to the Interest on Delayed Payments to Small Scale and Ancillary Industrial Undertakings Act, 1993
to bring down the existing time limit of 120 days is under active consideration of the Ministry of SSI.
Recommendation
4.2    Demand for re-defining of Factories Act, 1948
4.2.1The Committee was apprised by the SSI Associations and Ministry of SSI on the demand for re-defining of
Factories Act, 1948 and SSIs in terms of employment. The Committee understands that the National Commission of
Labour also recommended for enactment of the Bills on the Small Enterprises Employment which is under the
consideration of the Ministry of Labour. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the enactment of the Act should be
expedited.   (Para 60)
Action Taken
4.2.2The recommendations of Second National Commission on Labour in paragraphs 6.28 and 6.106 pertained to
enactment of a separate law, namely, the “Small Enterprises (Employment Relations) Act”. The Ministry of Labour and
Employment has informed that the matter has been examined. In view of the facts that (i) the Ministry of SSI is
contemplating to bring the “Small Enterprises Development Bill” which, inter alia, deals with labour matters, and (ii)
the Ministry of Labour and Employment is also proposing amendment to the “Labour Laws (Exemption from
Furnishing Returns and Maintaining Registers by Certain Establishments) Act, 1988” by expanding its scope and
coverage, there is no need to have a separate Small Enterprises (Employment Relations) Act.

by the Committee, hereby present this One Hundred Sixty third Report on the Action Taken by the Government on the

th Report on Credit Flow to SSI Sector in the region of

REPORT
         The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Small Scale Industries
on the Recommendations contained in the 147th Report (of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Industry) on Credit Flow to SSI Sector in the Region of Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh pertaining to the Ministry of
Small Scale Industries . The Report was presented /laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha on the 26th August,
2003.
2.      Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Small Scale Industries in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:
Chapter - I- The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry:- 43; 44 and 52
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendation as mentioned in Chapter -I of
the Report.
Chapter - II- The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the

Government’s replies:- 49 and 51
In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and explanation advocated by the
Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue further.
Chapter - III- The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies of the
Ministry:- 42; 46 and 48
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementations of recommendations contained in Chapter-III and
desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanation in respect of these recommendations.
Chapter - IV- The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry have not been
received:- 45; 47 and 50
         In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished the interim replies or
couched its language in vague terms like noted for compliance/guidance, recommendations have been forwarded to
Government of U. P. therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects
of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the
recommendations of the Committee.
3.      The details of the ATR is being discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.
CHAPTER - I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
Recommendation
1.0    Awareness amongst the SSI entrepreneurs about the various schemes/ facilities
1.1    The Committee understands that there is a lack of awareness amongst the SSI entrepreneurs about the various
schemes/ facilities being offered by the Government and financial institutions. It has resulted in largely under financing
of various schemes. The Committee therefore recommends that the Government and financial institutions should give
wide publicity and conduct awareness campaigns on the loan schemes amongst the SSI entrepreneurs so that the
benefits of various schemes percolate down to the grass root level. The Committee also directs that all the banks in the
area should invariably display in every branch the facilities being offered by them as well the websites of banks and
Government Organisations should be updated, especially in respect of the information regarding the Credit Guarantee
Fund Scheme.(Para 43)
Action Taken
1.1.1As decided at the second meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) on Flow of Institutional Credit to
SSI Sector, held on 3
rd April, 2002, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) advised the banks to display in their branch
premises, the limits up to which the collateral-free loans are available and other relevant information relating to
financing of the SSI sector. Subsequently, as decided at the third meeting of the SAC held on
15th January, 2003, it was reiterated to the banks that their branches should display the availability of collateral
free/composite loans, schemes like Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme/National Equity Fund / Credit Guarantee
Fund Scheme for Small Industries, time schedule for disposal of applications, etc. The RBI has informed that
compliance reports on this have been received from all public sector banks.
1.1.2Further, to increase awareness of the schemes/facilities to the SSI sector, the State Bank of India came out with a
“Charter for SSI” which was advertised in all leading newspapers. The Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) has also issued
circular dated 31st March, 2003 to all member banks to come out with similar charter for SSI sector. All 27 public sector
banks have issued “Charter for SSI”.
l.1.3  The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has been disseminating information on its schemes of
assistance among the SSI entrepreneurs through seminars/ workshops organized by various local industries associations,
besides the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Small & Medium Industries (FOSMI), etc. In order to
create greater awareness amongst SSI units, business campaigns/meets are organized at district headquarters, industry
centres and SSI clusters by the SIDBI. SSI entrepreneurs are given information on relevant schemes on one-to-one basis
during discussion on their projects. Besides, the salient features of all the schemes of the SIDBI are hosted on its

163rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/163rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:51:28]
website www.sidbi.com.
l.1.4  The CGTSI has also been taking necessary steps to publicise the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small
Industries and create awareness of the scheme among the member banks/lending institutions, SSI entrepreneurs and
other stakeholders. The CGTSI has forwarded posters on the Credit Guarantee Scheme to the Zonal Offices/Regional
Offices of the banks so that Branch Offices display the same for the SSI borrowers. Further, the advertisements relating
to the scheme have also been published in Hindi.
1.1.5Under its letter dated 15 th September, 2004, the RBI has informed that regular training programmes are being
organized by the banks for officers/staff so as to improve their work performance. In pursuance of the decisions taken at
the meeting of the Parliamentary Standing Committee held with the officials of banks/financial institutions during its
visit to Mumbai in June, 2001, RBI vide  its circular dated 14 th July, 2001 has advised all banks to conduct
entrepreneurship development training programmes and also give exhaustive training to their staff members sensitizing
them to the needs of the SSI sector. The feedback received from the banks shows that some banks have taken necessary
steps in this regard.
l.1.6  The IBA has forwarded the recommendation of the Committee to all public sector Member Banks for initiating
necessary action. As per the information received from the banks, various steps have been taken to enhance awareness
of the schemes/facilities being offered to SSI entrepreneurs, by way of publishing and posting on websites the “SSI
Charter”, printing and distribution of brochures/ pamphlets/ posters on schemes/ loan facilities for SSI for display at the
branches and conducting workshops, seminars, awareness campaigns, meetings with SSI Associations and training/
sensitization programmes for the Branch Managers/ Staff.
Recommendation
1.2    The Committee was informed that the SSI sector is under constant threat due to globalisation and their products
required to be marketed efficiently. The Committee appreciates the efforts and assistance extended by the NSIC.
However, the SSI Associations demand that in addition to their existing activities, the NSIC should organize exhibitions
for promoting the marketing of the goods produced in the area is justified. The Committee also feels that NSIC should
certainly help the SSIs in this respect. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the NSIC should come forward to
organize exhibitions for displaying products of the SSI units in various metros so as to enable to get more orders to
make viable the existing units which suffer from the under utilization of capacities for want of orders.(Para 44)
Action Taken
1.2.1The NSIC has established a permanent Display Centre to show case the products of SSI units at Okhla, New Delhi.
The SSI units from Khurja and adjoining areas have been provided facilities to display their products free of cost.
1.2.2The National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) in association with Kutir Chinni Patra Sangathan, Khurja,
SIDBI and SISI, organized on 22
nd September, 2003 an awareness campaign at Bulandshahr and 150 SSI units
participated in the event. 35 SSI units from Bulandshahr and adjoining areas participated in Handicrafts Expo’2004
exhibition organized by the NSIC at its Exhibition Centre in New Delhi during 12 th to l6th March, 2004 for which built-
up stalls were provided free of cost to the participating units.(Para 52)
Recommendation
1.3    There is no SSI bank branch in the district and it should be immediately set up. The normal bank branches are also
not located in all the industrial clusters. Each industrial area should have at least one branch. The Committee is of the
view that SSI branch exclusively to cater to the needs of the entrepreneurs and SSI units in the area be set up at the
earliest.
Action Taken
1.3.1The RBI has informed that as per the extant instructions, all banks (public sector banks, in particular) are required
to operationalise more specialised SSI branches to ensure that every district and SSI clusters within a district are served
by at least one specialised SSI bank branch. In view of the difficulties experienced by banks in opening full-fledged
specialised SSI branches due to lack of potential in any district, as per the decision of the Standing Advisory Committee
(SAC) on Flow of Institutional Credit to SSI Sector banks have been advised to categorise general banking branches
with more than 60 per cent advances to SSI sector as specialised SSI branches. As on 31
st March, 2004, the public
sector banks have 497 specialised SSI branches all over the country.

163rd Report of Committee on Industry

1.3.2The RBI’s Regional Office at Lucknow has advised the three major banks in the region, viz., Punjab National
Bank, State Bank of India and Oriental Bank of Commerce to examine the feasibility of opening specialised SSI
branches in each of the industrial clusters in the region. They have also advised the Convenor to the District
Consultative Committee for Bulandshahr to discuss the issue at the District Consultative Committee (DCC) and District
Level Review Committee (DLRC) meetings. The Punjab National Bank has informed that to provide timely and
adequate credit to the SSI units, it has set up specialized SSI Credit Cell at Lead District Main Branch, Civil Lines,
Bulandshahr, Branch Office at Sikandrabad Industrial Area and Branch Office at Khurja.
CHAPTER - II
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO
PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
Recommendation
2.0    Milk cooperative sector
         The Committee notes that taking into account the quantum of milk produced in the district which is next to Gujarat
and is in the non-cooperative sector, there is a strong demand for an organisational support for procurement, processing
and transportation of the milk and also to provide the best price to the producers. The Committee therefore, recommends
that considering the quantum of milk produced the Government should provide necessary support either through
cooperative sector or by setting up a public sector unit to tap the potential available in the area in an organized manner.
(Para 49)
Action Taken
2.1    The Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying has informed that Bulandshahr
district in Uttar Pradesh was covered under the Operation Flood Project. The milk production in Bulandshahr was
estimated to be 24.38 lakh litres per day in 2003. The District Cooperative Milk Producers Union in Bulandshahr has
868 functioning primary milk cooperative societies, which serve about 87 per cent of l,103 (revenue) villages in the
district. The District Union collects more than one lakh litres of milk per day. The milk processing capacity of the Union
is 60 thousand litres per day and chilling capacity 80 thousand litres per day. Further, a large number of private dairy
plants are located in the district, with an estimated total capacity of approximately 21 lakh litres for milk processing and
7 lakh litres for milk chilling per day.
Recommendation
2.2    Attaching Bulandshahr with NSIC in Delhi
2.2.1As regards the support from the NSIC it was demanded that this district should be attached to Delhi instead of
Agra. The NSIC may identify at least five units in consultation with the District Industries Officer and project them as
model for others to follow. The Committee is of the view that the Government should explore the possibilities to attach
Bulandshahr with Delhi instead of Agra so as to encourage the entrepreneurs. It is also of the view that the NSIC should
develop some units in consultation with the DIO as model units.(Para 51)
Action Taken
2.2.2As informed by the NSIC, Bulandshahr district is serviced by NSIC Zonal Office at NOIDA. However, technical
inspection of SSI units from Bulandshahr area under the Single Point Registration Scheme for Government Stores
Purchase Programme is being referred to the Small Industries Service Institute (SISI), Agra.
CHAPTER - III
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT
ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation
3.0    Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Small Industries (CGFTST)
3.1    The Committee is constrained to note that benefit of the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Small Industries (CGFT)
are not reaching to the SSI entrepreneurs. The Committee recommends that the Government and the SIDBI to ensure

163rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/163rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:51:28]
that all the requisite steps be taken for its success and an action taken report be furnished to Committee within three
months.(Para 42)
Action Taken
3.1.1The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Small Industries (CGTSI) has been making continuous efforts for creating
awareness about the Credit Guarantee Scheme since its inception. For this purpose, it has been organizing region-wise
seminars/programmes for the Member Lending Institutions (MLIs), i.e., commercial banks, etc., to explain the details of
the scheme and benefits available to both MLIs and small enterprises. The CGTSI has also been deputing its officials to
workshops/ training programmes organized by the MLIs for their Credit officials to explain the procedure of lodging
applications under the Scheme and other operational modalities. Further, CGTSI/SIDBI officials have been participating
in exhibitions/ fairs and attending seminars and other programmes /meetings organized/convened by the SSI
Associations and Central/State Government Departments besides, the State Level Inter-Institutional Committee (SLIIC)
and State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) meetings, etc. Till December, 2004, CGTSI has participated in around 273
such seminars/ workshops-cum-training programmes/meetings/exhibitions/fairs throughout the country and provided
information on the Credit Guarantee Scheme to various stakeholders. Through such concerted efforts, the awareness
levels in MLIs/Industry have shown a distinct improvement, which is reflected in the increased coverage by MLIs under
the scheme.
3.1.2As on 3lst December, 2004, 21,234 proposals involving aggregate credit amount of Rs. 419.90 crore, have been
approved under the Credit Guarantee Scheme on an all ­India basis. Out of this, 6,458 proposals involving credit
amount of around Rs. 38 crore pertain to Uttar Pradesh. The number of proposals covered in Uttar Pradesh is the highest
among all the States. From Bulandshahr district, 18 proposals involving credit amount of around Rs. 35.24 lakh have so
far been covered under the Credit Guarantee Scheme.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3The Committee notes that eighteen proposals involving credit amount of Rs. 35.24 lakh have so far been covered
under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Bulandshahr. However, the Committee is of the view that there is a need to
broaden the base of Credit Guarantee Scheme for accelerated proliferation of small enterprises in the country. The
Committee endorses that Bulandshahr is one of the commercial centre of U.P. and recommends that concerted efforts
should be taken to cover more cases under credit guarantee scheme.
Recommendation
3.2    Declining trend in credit flow to SSIs
3.2.1The Committee is very much concerned about the declining trend in credit flow to SSIs. The steps taken by the
Ministry of SSI to enhance credit flow to SSI sector are not adequate. The Committee is of the view that non
compliance of the RBI guidelines is the major reason which has resulted in the decline of credit flow. The Committee,
therefore, impress upon the Government to take serious measures to arrest this trend. Further, the Committee
recommends that the Standard Advisory Committee on Credit Flow should be given more powers to monitor the
situation and advise the Government in this regard.
(Para 46)
Action Taken
3.2.2The flow of credit to SSI sector from the public sector banks has gone up from Rs. 29,482 crore in March, 1996 to
Rs. 58,277 crore in March, 2004 (provisional available data) in absolute terms. However, credit to SSI sector, as
percentage to Net Bank Credit (NBC), has come down mainly because the rate of growth in advances to SSI sector is
not commensurate with the rate of growth in NBC. This issue was deliberated in the meeting of the Parliamentary
Standing Committee with the CMDs of public sector banks and SIDBI held on 10
th January, 2005. The Ministry of SSI
has been taking up the problems faced by the SSI sector in credit flow from the banks/ institutional sources with the
RBI’s Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) from time to time and based on the decisions taken, the banks have been
advised by the RBI to take the needful action accordingly.
3.2.3To ensure adequate credit flow to SSI sector, the Government and RBI have taken various measures which inter
alia include simplified procedure for computing the working capital requirement of SSI units on the basis of minimum
20 per cent of the projected annual turnover of the borrowing unit for limits up to
Rs. 5 crore, advising the banks to fix self-set target for growth in advances to SSI sector, fixing time frame for disposal
of loan applications, enhancement in composite loan limit from Rs.50 lakh to Rs. 1 crore, dispensing with collateral

163rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/163rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:51:28]
security requirement for loans up to Rs. 25 lakh to SSI units having good track record and financial position,
enhancement of credit limit under Laghu Udhyami Credit Card (LUCC) from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh based on
satisfactory track record, etc.
3.2.4As announced by the Government, a Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Fund has been structured by SIDBI
with an initial envisaged corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore spread over 2 years, i.e., FY 2005 and FY 2006 for providing
impetus to the growth of SME sector. The interest rate on assistance out of the Fund has been kept concessional and
competitive at up to 2 per cent below SIDBI’s PLR, which at present works out to up to 9.5 per cent per annum.
3.2.5As regards the recommendation that more powers be given to the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to monitor
the situation and advise the Government, it may be stated that the Committee is chaired by a Deputy Governor of the
RBI. The Secretary, Ministry of SSI; Secretary, Ministry of Finance; Chairman, National Bank for Agriculture and
Rural Development (NABARD); Executive Director in-charge of Rural Planning and Credit Department, RBI;
Chairman, SIDBI; Chairman, State Bank of India and Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) are
its permanent members. The Public Sector Banks, State Financial Corporations (SFCs) and SSI Associations are also
represented on this Committee by rotation. The Committee holds meetings regularly to review the flow of credit to the
SSI sector and problems faced by the sector in securing adequate flow of credit and to suggest improvements in the
procedures and modifications in the policies. The action taken on the decisions of the Committee are deliberated upon
and monitored at the subsequent meetings.
Further Recommendation
3.2.6The Committee knows that the flow of credit to SSI sector from the public sector banks has gone up Rs. 29,482
crore in March, 1996 to Rs. 58,277 crore in March, 2004 but the percentage of net bank credit to SSI sector has come
down from seventeen per cent in 1998 to almost ten per cent in 2004 because of the fact that the rate of growth in
advances to SSI sector is not commensurate with the rate of growth in net bank credit. This is the main concern of the
Committee which has been expressed by the Committee during the course of the meetings held on 1
st September, 2004,
10th January, 3rd March, 2005 with the representatives of nationalized banks and Banking Division. The same issue was
discussed in detail in the meeting of Sub-Committee for Ministry of Small Scale Industries (of Standing Committee on
Industry) held on 19th March and 11th April, 2005 with the select nationalized banks. In the meeting held on 11 th April,
2005, the SSI Associations, also hailing from Bulandshahr, expressed their resentment and anguish over the inadequate
credit flow to SSI sector.
3.2.7The Committee expresses its deepest concern over the pathetic credit flow to SSI sector in general and in the region
of Bulandshahr and is of the considered view that the declining trend of percentage to net bank credit to SSI sector
needs to be arrested at the earliest rather it needs to be reversed to almost to the level of 17 to 18 per cent, if the goal of
12 per cent growth rate in the SSI sector as the target set in 10th Five Year Plan is to be achieved.
Recommendation
3.3    Roads and transport facilities
3.3.1The Committee was also informed that the roads and transport facilities are grossly inadequate and the district has
no direct railway link. Moreover, by-pass roads are required to resolve the problem of traffic jam in Dadri and
Sikendrabad towns in the district. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government of India should extend
necessary support to the State Government of Uttar Pradesh to develop the necessary road and rail links for proper
growth of SSIs in the area.
(Para 48)
Action Taken
3.3.2This matter was taken up with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MORTH) and the Ministry of
Railways for appropriate action. The MORTH has informed that the National Highway No. 91 (Ghaziabad-Kanpur
Road) is not a four-lane road throughout and around Dadri town, there is often traffic congestion. That Ministry is
considering expanding the width of this section of the highway to four-lane. The State PWD has also submitted certain
proposals for relieving congestion on this highway which is at present under that Ministry’s consideration. The traffic
congestion around Sikandrabad town on this highway is also in the knowledge of the MORTH. In consultation with the
State Government of U.P., that Ministry is considering ways to expand the road width to relieve traffic congestion.

163rd Report of Committee on Industry
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/163rdreport.htm[04-07-2016 12:51:28]
Further Recommendation
3.3.3The Ministry of SSI should take up the issue of direct railway link to Bulandshahr for the betterment of SSI sector
and making the city commercially viable. Moreover, adequate follow up action should be taken with Ministry of Road
Transport and Highways (MORTH) for immediate expanding the width of National Highway No. 91 (Ghaziabad-
Kanpur road) into at least a four lane road so that the traffic problem in Dadri and Sikandrabad town in resolved for the
smooth transportation of SSI products.
CHAPTER - IV
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH
FINAL REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation
4.0    Constitution of the Committee by the lead bank
4.1    The Committee took note of the complaints of the apathetic attitude of the officers and staff of the State
Government and banks. The entrepreneurs are harassed in the guise of rules and procedures and thus setting up of an
unit becomes a Herculean task. The Committee strongly feels that it has to be done away with if industry has to grow. It
is therefore required that a Committee be set up by the lead bank i.e., Punjab National Bank consisting of Banks’
representatives, Director of Industries, local MP’s and MLA’s and members of the SSI associations to resolve the
problems of SSI entrepreneurs and monitor the lending of loans. This Committee should meet quarterly to review the
position. The Committee therefore recommends for constitution of the said Committee at the earliest.(Para 45)
Action Taken
4.1.2The RBI has informed that instructions already exist for simplification of procedural formalities and simplified
application forms for sanction of loans to SSI entrepreneurs. To make available timely credit to the SSI sector, a time
frame has been fixed for disposal of loan applications, viz., up to Rs. 25,000/- within 2 weeks and up to            Rs. 5
lakh, within 4 weeks provided the loan applications are complete in all respects and accompanied by a ‘check list’.
Further, the RBI has issued “Guidelines on Fair Practices Code for Lenders” to all banks and all-India Financial
Institutions for their implementation. In addition, to reduce hardship being faced by the SSI entrepreneurs in      securing
term loan and working capital from separate financial institutions/banks, the banks have been advised to extend
composite loans (the limit for which has been recently enhanced from Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 1 crore) through a single
window so that the entire financing requirement is met by single documentation and security/charge creation process.
4.1.3As regards setting up of a Committee to look into the problems of the entrepreneurs under the lead bank in the
district, the RBI has stated that in each district there are two fora, viz., the District Consultative Committee (DCC)) and
District Level Review Committee (DLRC) which hold meetings quarterly to review the position of credit flow to
different sectors, including credit flow to SSI sector. Elected public representatives (MPs/ MLAs) are also invited to
participate in discussion in the DLRC meetings.
4.1.4The recommendation of the Committee has been forwarded to the Government of Uttar Pradesh for taking
appropriate action. The IBA has also forwarded the recommendation of the Committee to all public sector Member
Banks for initiating necessary action. The Punjab National Bank has informed that its Regional Office, Bulandshahr is
being advised to set up a Committee to solve the problems of SSI entrepreneurs.

CREDIT GUARANTEE FUND TRUST FOR SMALL INDUSTRIES (CGFT)
         The Committee notes that eighteen proposals involving credit amount of Rs. 35.24 lakh have so far been covered
under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Bulandshahar. However, the Committee is of the view that there is a need to
broaden the base of Credit Guarantee Scheme for accelerated proliferation of small enterprises in the country. The
Committee endorses that Bulandshahar is one of the commercial centre of U.P. and recommends that concerted efforts
should be taken to cover more cases under credit guarantee scheme.(3.1.3)
DECLINING TREND IN CREDIT FLOW TO SSIS
         The Committee knows that the flow of credit to SSI sector from the public sector banks has gone up Rs. 29,482
crore in March, 1996 to Rs. 58,277 crore in March, 2004 but the percentage of net bank credit to SSI sector has come
down from seventeen per cent in 1998 to almost ten per cent in 2004 because of the fact that the rate of growth in
advances to SSI sector is not commensurate with the rate of growth in net bank credit. This is the main concern of the
Committee which has been expressed by the Committee during the course of the meetings held on 1
st September, 2004,
10th January, 3rd March, 2005 with the representatives of nationalized banks and Banking Division. The same issue was
discussed in detail in the meeting of Sub-Committee for Ministry of Small Scale Industries (of Standing Committee on
Industry) held on 19
th March and 11th April, 2005 with the select nationalized banks. In the meeting held on 11 th April,

credit flow to SSI sector        (3.2.6)

region of Bulandshahar and is of the considered view that the declining trend of percentage to net bank credit to SSI
sector needs to be arrested at the earliest rather it needs to be reversed to almost to the level of 17 to 18 per cent, if the
goal of 12 per cent growth rate in the SSI sector as the target set in TenthFive Year Plan is to be
achieved.                          (3.2.7)

sector and making the city commercially viable. Moreover, adequate follow up action should be taken with Ministry of
Road Transport and Highways (MORTH) for immediate expanding the width of National Highway No. 91 (Ghaziabad
Kanpur road) into at least a four lane road so that the traffic problem in Dadri and Sikandrabad town in resolved for the
smooth transportation of SSI
products.                                                                                                                                         (3.3.3)

authorised by the Committee, hereby present this One Hundred Sixty four Report on the Action Taken by the
Government on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s 150" Report on Demands for Grants
(2004-05) pertaining to Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises)

2. The Committee examined and considered the Action Taken Notes supplied by the Government (Ministry
of Small Scale Industries) on the recommendations contained in its 150" Report on Demands for Grants
(2004-05) pertaining to Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises)

REPORT

The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Public
Enterprises (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises) on the recommendations contained in the
150th Report (of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry) on Demands for
Grants (2004-05) pertaining to Department of Public Enterprises. The Report was presented /laid on the
Table of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha on the 26th August, 2004

2 Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries in respect of
the recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:

Chapter-I— The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry :-
Paras:- 45; 56; 570); 57(ii); 57 (iii); 57 (iv) and 57(vi)

The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as mentioned
in Chapter-I of the Report.

Chapter-II— The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of
the Government’s replies:-
Paras :- 10; 33; 41 and 52.

In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and explanation
advocated by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue further.

Chapter-III— The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies
of the Ministry: -
Paras:- 6; 13; 16; 17; 24; 26; 27; 35; 36; 49; 50; 51; 53; 57 (v) and 57 (ii).

The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendations contained in
Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanation in respect of these recommendations.

Chapter-IV—The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry have
not been received:-

Paras :- 34; 38 and 55.

In respect of recommendations in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished the interim replies or
couched its language in vague terms like noted for compliance/guidance, therefore, the Committee desires
that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respect of recommendations categorized in Chapter-
IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.

3. The Details of the ATR is being discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.


CHAPTER -1
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNME

Recommendation
1.0 Displaced employee needs psychological counselling

1.1 The Committee expresses its concern that the displaced employee needs psychological counselling to
absorb the trauma of loss of job and to face the new circumstances. They need advice for the prudent
management of their compensation amount and other financial benefits from the CPSU. They also need to be
made aware of the new environment of market opportunities so that they may, depending upon his aptitude
and expertise, take up economic activities.

(Para No 45)

Action Taken

1.1.1 The Consultant appointed to undertake the efficacy study of the CRR Scheme has submitted its report,
which also contains the above views of the Committee. A concerted effort will be initiated alongwith compliance
of other recommendations of the consultant.

Recommendation
1.2 Recommendations of Expenditure Reform Commission

1.2.1 The Committee observes that the recommendations of Expenditure Reform Commission regarding the
existence of Department of Public Enterprises may be viewed considering the activities, achievements and
proposed plans of the Department. The Committee is of the view that the effective implementation of these
plans is of critical importance for success of current economic reforms.

(Para 56)

Action Taken

1.2.2 Recommendations of the ERC have been examined in the Department in consultation with SCOPE
with regard to preparation of PE Survey Work and Ministry of Law regarding PMA. While Ministry of Law
has stated that taking back PMA from DPE will hamper the work whereas SCOPE has regretted their
inability to undertake the PE Survey Work. Department is of the view that the transferring of MOU work to
administrative Ministries /Department will erode the neutrality of the MOU work. Since there was a diversion
of views of DPE and ERC representation, the matter was taken up with Committee of Secretaries with the
request that DPE may be allowed to continue to act as a nodal Ministry of CPSUs. COS has now advised this
Department to take the matter with Department of Expenditure in this regard. Accordingly, the matter is

_ being taken up with expenditure. However, Government has also decided to set up Board for Reconstruction
of Public Sector Enterprises which should be administered under DPE. Once it is approved by the
Government, the work of DPE is bound to increase and the role of DPE will also be vital and the staff
strength would need to be increased. The recommendations of ERC regarding DPE would need to be reviewed
appropriately.


Recommendation
1.3. Financial and functional autonomy

1.3.1 Initiatives for policy planning in providing financial and functional autonomy to the CPSEs in order to
help make them globally competitive.
[Para 57(i)]

Action Taken

1.3.2 Government has already given enhanced powers to Navratna CPSEs way back in 1997. Since the
Government has pledged in its National Common Minimum Programme to devolve full managerial and
commercial autonomy to successful profit making companies operating in competitive environment action
has already been taken in this direction for providing enhanced financial powers to the Boards of successful
profit making CPSEs operating in a competitive environment. Apart from enhancing the financial ceiling on
investment, powers for merger and acquisition, approval of foreign business tours etc. are also proposed to
be delegated. 7

Recommendation
1.4 Revival/reconstruction/restructuring/closure of the sick/loss making CPSEs

1.4.1 Initiatives for the revival/reconstruction/restructuring/closure of the sick/loss making CPSEs including
decisions related to disinvestments by the administrative Ministries/departments should be in consultation
with DPE.

[Para 57(ii)]

Action Taken

1.4.2 The Government has since decided to establish a Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises
(BRPSE), to be located in the Department of Public Enterprises. The Board will, among other things, examine
proposals of the administrative Ministries for revival/restructuring of sick/loss making CPSEs for their turn
around, advise the Government on disinvestment/closure/sale of chronically sick/loss making companies
which cannot be revived, monitor incipient sickness, etc. Department of Public Enterprises has to provide
secretariat assistance to the Board.

Recommendation
1.5 Changing industrial and business scenario

1.5.1 Constant review of the guidelines in line with changing industrial and business scenario so as to
facilitate the CPSEs in fulfilling their commercial and social objectives in a prompt and competitive manner.
[Para 57(iii)]

Action Taken

1.5.2 The guidelines issued by DPE/BPE are reviewed from time to time. As a result of their reviews 696
guidelines were cancelled in 1997and another 77 guidelines were deleted in 2003. This process of review is
ongoing.

Recommendation
1.6 Use of information system

1.6.1 Enhanced use of information system i.e. web based computer applications, networking etc.
[Para 57(iv)]


Action Taken

1.6.2 All the sections of DPE have been provided computers and have the = of internet facilities. There
is a Local Area Network (LAN) operational in the Department. Department has proposed to undertake
following steps in this direction:

(i) Impetus on use of LAN Based Intra-Departmental Communication.
(ii) Publication such as “DPE’s Overview” for international circulation.
(iii) Upgradation of H/W for various officers.
(iv) Use of latest virus protection s/w for greater data security.
Recommendation
1.7 Focus on social safety net schemes

1.7.1 The Committee recommends greater focus on social safety net schemes i.e. counselling, retraining and
redeployment scheme and promoting it wider coverage.
[Para No. 57 (vi)]

Action Taken

1.7.2 There has been continuous focus on widening the network of the social safety net scheme, 1.6.
Counselling, Retraining and Redeployment Scheme for the rationalized employees of Central PSUs. Initially,
when the scheme was introduced in the year 2001-02, there were 17 nodal agencies. Presently, there are 34
such agencies having more than 100 Employees Assistance Centres located all over the country to meet the
demand of training under the scheme. Based on need, nodal agencies and their centres are added.

|


CHAPTER - II

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO
PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES

Recommendation
2.0 One time comprehensive package

2.1 The committee, therefore, recommends that one time comprehensive package should be given to the
PSEs which should be enjoined with accountability clause on the part of management.
(Para No. 10)

Action Taken

2.1.1 DPE does not directly deal with restructuring packages. Such exercise is done by the concerned
administrative Ministries/Departments. Hence, the recommendation of the Committee has been brought to
the notice of these Ministries/Departments for taking appropriate action vide DPE’s O.M. No. DPE. 4(3)/
2004- Fin. dated the 20% September, 2004.

Recommendation
2.2 Financial parameters and the targets

2.2.1 The Committee observes that MOU system has been relevant in the past and still holds relevance in the
current scenario though it needs a review. It is desirable if the weightage given to the financial parameters is
significant and the targets should be sufficiently high with a view to improve performance and productivity,
year after year.

(Para No. 33)

Action Taken

2.2.2 In the MOU guidelines for the year 2004-05, 50% weight has been assigned to financial parameters. In
order to ensure sufficiently high targets, it has been stipulated that Budget Estimates (BE) should be placed in
“Good” column and that the differential between Excellent and Very Good targets column should be around
15% and 5% .

Recommendation
2.3. Corrective measures for improvement of PSEs whose performance was graded as Poor

2.3.1 The Committee also desires to have some feedback/report from the PSEs who have signed MOU
particularly those who have been graded as excellent or poor. Such a feedback will help the Committee to
assess the strengths of MOU system and the constraints some PSEs are still facing. The Committee also
secks the Department’s view on the PSEs that have been graded as Poor. Does the Department suggest any
corrective measures for such PSEs. 7
(Para No. 35)

Action Taken

2.3.2 The Department of Public Enterprises does not suggest any corrective actions for PSEs which are
rated as Poor as these corrective actions are to be undertaken by the concerned Administrative Ministry/



Department. All issues related to the performance of the PSEs are discussed in detail during the MOU
negotiation meeting where the Task Force Members also discuss and suggest about the various strategies to
improve the performance of particular PSE.

Recommendation
2.4 Obligations on the part of Government

2.4.1 The Committee further desires to be apprised about the obligations on the part of Government as the
contracting party signing the MOU.
(Para 36)

Action Taken

2.4.2 The obligations on the part of Government as the contracting party are included as a separate chapter
in the MOU. These are related to the nature and operations of the particular PSE and therefore vary from
company to company.

Recommendation
2.5 Speedy settlement of disputes

2.5.1 The Committce considers it to be a positive initiative. It desires to be apprised of the impact of this
mechanism in speedy settlement of disputes.
(Para 41)

Action Taken

2.5.2 Permanent Machinery of Arbitrators has been set up in Department of Public Enterprises for ‘resolving
commercial disputes except taxation between PSEs inter-se as well as between a PSE and a Central Government
Department/Ministry. From 1993-94 disputes with Port Trusts have also been included under the purview of
PMA for arbitration, and the Ministry of Railways were excluded from the purview of PMA vide DPE OM
dated 12.2.97. All the disputes between the PSUs are required to be referred to Department of Public Enterprises
for its reference to the Arbitrator of PMA. Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises on being satisfied
with prima facie existence of dispute, refers the dispute to the Arbitrator of the PMA for Arbitration. The
Arbitration Act, 1940 is not applicable in these cases. No lawyer is allowed to appear on behalf of either party
for presenting/defending the cases, however they may use their own lawyers who are under their employ.
This saves the PSUs from paying unnecessary money to lawyers when the disputing parties involved are
PSUs. The PSU’s are not supposed to go to court, their cases are settled by the Arbitrator of PMA. This
avoid the delay caused in courts and helps in early settlement of their disputes. Ever since the PMA was set
up in 1989, 183 disputes have been received, out of which 102 cases have been settled.

Recommendation
2.6 Facilitics of medical, educational and other social securities

2.6.1 The Committee recommends that the facilities of medical, educational and other social securities should
remain available to the former employees in respective PSEs.
(Para 52)

Action Taken

2.6.2 As regards making available the medical facilities to the former employees of CPSEs, DPE have already
directed the CPSEs vide Para 13 of DPE OM No. 2(49)/98 DPE(WC) 25.6.99 to look into the mediclaim
cover through Insurance Companies for their retired employees.


2.6.3 Regarding the educational and other social securities to the former employees of CPSEs, DPE have not
formulated any scheme in the matter as these facilities are to be evolved and implemented by the concerned
managements of the CPSEs.



= - Til

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT
ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY

Recommendation
3.0 DPE’s role as the nodal Department for all the CPSEs

3.1 The Committee acknowledges DPE’s role as the nodal Department for all the CPSEs and as such its
importance inthe economic development of the country. While specific action is to be taken by the concerned
administrative Ministry, DPE provides policy framework and facilitates atmosphere for better productivity,
smooth functioning and higher contribution to national economy.

(Para 6)

Action Taken

3.1.1 The Department of Public Enterprises acts as the nodal Department for all Central PSEs and assists in
the formulation of policy pertaining to performance evaluation, autonomy and financial delegation, personnel
management, human resource development of CPSEs. DPE will continue to extend all policy support to
CPSEs for creating atmosphere conducive to improving the efficiency of CPSEs.

Further Recommendation

3.1.2 The Committee is of the view that the Department of Public Enterprises must assume its
responsibility in order to discharge its function as per its mandate and according to the changing
corporate environment and the domestic economic reality caused duc to globalisation and liberlisation.
It is because of the pivotal importance of its function that the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Industry had recommended in its earlier report for strengthening of the
Department of Public Enterprises. It is now the time for the Department of Public Enterprises to
prove its raison-deter/justification for its continuation as separate Department. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department of Public Enterprise should undertake following activities
effectively:-

(i) Review of parameter under MoU system for performance evaluation as per global trend ;

Gi) Determination of level of functional autonomy and linking the same with performance
with mode of periodic review;

(iii) fixation of delegation of financial power as per requirement of corporate world;

(iv) Evaluation of existing human resources in al! Central PSUs and determine parameters
and premises for Comprehensive Human Resource Planning and Management including
induction of professionalisation at all levels of management.

3.1.3 The Committee desires that Department of Public Enterprises must come out with concrete
actions taken on above issues and accordingly apprise the Committee in its action taken note of the
present report.


Recommendation
3.2 Pian allocation for IT sector

3.2.1 The Committee concurs with the plan allocation for IT sector, and hopes that it would result in
improvement of efficiency of the Department. As the Department functions as the centralized coordinating
unit for all the CPSEs, the IT would be useful for maintaining a comprehensive database for all the stakeholders.
The Committee further suggests for creation of an exclusive website for the CRR scheme to create and
maintain a comprehensive database for the use of all the stakeholders.

(Para 13)

Action Taken

3.2.2 Efforts have been initiated to create a website for CRR Scheme and the details are being worked out by
the NIC.

Further Recommendation

3.2.3 The Committee is of the view that the Department of Public Enterprises have been entrusted
with significant responsibility without adequate secretariat structure causing delay in the
accomplishment of its duties. The Department seems to have remained under the shadow of
Department of Heavy Industry. This Department has been entrusted with enormous responsibility
for co-ordinating and managing the affairs of Central PSEs, which is called in Nehruvian term, the
“Temple of Modern India”. The Department acts as nodal agency and is supposed to lay down the
policy guidelines on performance improvement and evaluation, financial accounting and provides an
inter-face between the administrative Ministries and PSEs. Therefore, the Committee recommends
that the Department should be strengthened and adequately staffed.

Recommendation
3.3 Policy for Economic Development for North Eastern Region

3.3.1 The Committce recommends that extensive initiative by the DPE must be taken in consonance with the
overall policy for economic development for North Eastern Region. As such the Department should take
concerted initiatives with Ministry of the Development of North Eastern region.

(Para 16)

Action Taken

3.3.2 DPE is making all efforts to strengthen the CRR. Scheme in N.E. Region. In view of existing
difficulties and adversities in implementation of the scheme in the region, this Department has taken up the
matter with Planning Commission for granting special dispensation so as to allow the agencies in this
region to start residential programmes at higher norms for the VR optees to attract more and more number
of trainees.

Further Recommendation

3.3.3 While the Committee appreciates the efforts undertaken by the Department of Public
Enterprises in the strengthening of CRR Scheme in the NER, however, the Committee would like to
know the outcome of efforts of the Department for taking up the issue with the Planning
Commissioner on granting special dispensation for starting residential programme for the VR optees
to attracts large number of trainees. The Committee would like to know the details of number of
ben aries under the scheme and their post training engagement during last 5 years alongwith
details of expenses incurred thereon.



Recommendation
3.4 CRR scheme should cover the traditional industrics

3.4.1 The Committee further observes that in view of rich natural resources and traditional industries of this
region, the CRR scheme should cover the traditional industries, agro-based, small scale and cottage industry
specific to the region. The region has vast potential of tourism. Rationalized employees of this region may
be involved in such region-specific industries. In view of the geographical, climatic and environmental
factors IT based enterprises have great potential in the NE region. The Committee recommends that the
Government should ensure that IT potential is suitably exploited.

(Para No. 17)

Action Taken

3.4.2 The nodal agencies cngaged to undertake training programme in Guwahati under CRR Scheme offer
different type of EDP courses in Food Processing , Marketing Strategy for rural entrepreneurship products,

3.5 Effect of Miniratna Status

3.5.1 The Committee desires DPE to furnish an appraisal of the effect of such (Miniratna) status and directs

Action Taken

3.5.2 There are established mechanisms for monitoring of the performance of Miniratna PSEs. These are as
under:

(i) Board of Directors and Committees of the Board (Audit Committee, etc.) - continuous and regular
basis

(ii) Team consisting of Secretary of the administrative Ministry, Chief Executive of the PSU and one
or more outside expert - quarterly basis.

(iii) Inter-Ministerial Group consisting of Secretary, DPE, Secretary, Planning Commission, Secretary
(Expenditure) and the Secretary of the administrative Ministry concerned.

3.5.3 The Inter-Ministerial Group had reviewed the performance of all the Miniratna PSEs during 2003-04.
The IMG has observed that the introduction of the Scheme of Miniratna has resulted in the delegation of
enhanced autonomy and financial and operational powers to these PSUs and they are in a position to take
decisions quickly, reduce cost and time over-run and to set up joint ventures/subsidiaries. Further, Board
restructuring has resulted in the professionalisation of Boards. The existing schemes of delegation of powers
to Miniratna is being reviewed and suitable proposals being made to CCEA for approval.

Further Recommendation

3.5.4 The Committee is not disputing the criteria and mode of performance evaluation of Miniratna
PSEs by the Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) and the Committee is also in agreements with IMG that
the introduction of the scheme of the Miniratna resulting into delegation of financial and operational
power to PSEs might have benefited the PSEs due to enhanced autonomy. So far so good. But the
effect of the introduction of the scheme of Miniratna must have a bearing on the performance of the
PSEs. Therefore, the success of instruments of Miniratna depend largely upon the evaluation of
enhanced performance of PSEs which have been so awarded as Miniratna status. Then and only
then, the benefits of delegation of financial and operational powers backed by so acclaimed financial
autonomy could be examined in appropriate perspective. Moreover, the membership of Miniratna
status should not remain a permanent feature, rather there should be a dynamic and vibrating
membership system wherein the actual/physical and financial performance should be the guiding
consideration for awarding and de-reserving the status of Miniratna.

(Para No.26)

Action Taken

3.6.2 The Search .Committee had earlier made recommendations for appointment of non-official Directors
on the Boards of the remaining Miniratna PSEs also and these are with the concerned administrative Ministries/

Search Committee. The concerned administrative Ministries/Departments have been advised to take necessary
action to appoint non-official Directors in all these PSEs following the due procedure.

its function in relation to Board structure and its professionalisation of central PSEs. The Committee
during its study visits and interaction with select PSEs has found that post of part-time non-official
directors (say in CCL, HEC, NALCO, Hindustan Copper Ltd., HAL etc.) have remained vacant for

professionalisation of Board of Directors and functional autonomy as a result of delegation of financial
and operational power, however, on the other hand, it is found that the posts of part-time non-
official directors remain vacant for years. Under the circumstances, the functioning of the Board of

directors of central PSEs to commensurate the acclaimed professionalisation and functional
autonomy:

responsibility in order to discharge its function as per its mandate and according to the changing
corporate environment and the domestic economic reality caused due to globalisation and liberlisation.
